classes.label: 3DModel
classes.definition: A 3D model represents some kind of 3D content, which may have [[encoding]]s in one or more [[MediaObject]]s. Many 3D formats are available (e.g. see [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:3D_graphics_file_formats)); specific encoding formats can be represented using the [[encodingFormat]] property applied to the relevant [[MediaObject]]. For the case of a single file published after Zip compression, the convention of appending '+zip' to the [[encodingFormat]] can be used. Geospatial, AR/VR, artistic/animation, gaming, engineering and scientific content can all be represented using [[3DModel]].

classes.label: AMRadioChannel
classes.definition: A radio channel that uses AM.

classes.label: APIReference
classes.definition: Reference documentation for application programming interfaces (APIs).

classes.label: AboutPage
classes.definition: Web page type: About page.

classes.label: AcceptAction
classes.definition:
The act of committing to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

* [[RejectAction]]: The antonym of AcceptAction.

classes.label: Accommodation
classes.definition:
An accommodation is a place that can accommodate human beings, e.g. a hotel room, a camping pitch, or a meeting room. Many accommodations are for overnight stays, but this is not a mandatory requirement. For more specific types of accommodations not defined in schema.org, one can use [[additionalType]] with external vocabularies.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: AccountingService
classes.definition: Accountancy business.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

classes.label: AchieveAction
classes.definition: The act of accomplishing something via previous efforts. It is an instantaneous action rather than an ongoing process.

classes.label: Action
classes.definition: An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/04/16/announcing-schema-org-actions/) and [Actions overview document](https://schema.org/docs/actions.html).

classes.label: ActionAccessSpecification
classes.definition: A set of requirements that must be fulfilled in order to perform an Action.

classes.label: ActionStatusType
classes.definition: The status of an Action.

classes.label: ActivateAction
classes.definition: The act of starting or activating a device or application (e.g. starting a timer or turning on a flashlight).

classes.label: AddAction
classes.definition: The act of editing by adding an object to a collection.

classes.label: AdministrativeArea
classes.definition: A geographical region, typically under the jurisdiction of a particular government.

classes.label: AdultEntertainment
classes.definition: An adult entertainment establishment.

classes.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumeration of considerations that make a product relevant or potentially restricted for adults only.

classes.label: AdvertiserContentArticle
classes.definition: An [[Article]] that an external entity has paid to place or to produce to its specifications. Includes [advertorials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertorial), sponsored content, native advertising and other paid content.

classes.label: AggregateOffer
classes.definition: When a single product is associated with multiple offers (for example, the same pair of shoes is offered by different merchants), then AggregateOffer can be used.\n\nNote: AggregateOffers are normally expected to associate multiple offers that all share the same defined [[businessFunction]] value, or default to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell if businessFunction is not explicitly defined.

classes.label: AggregateRating
classes.definition: The average rating based on multiple ratings or reviews.

classes.label: AgreeAction
classes.definition: The act of expressing a consistency of opinion with the object. An agent agrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

classes.label: Airline
classes.definition: An organization that provides flights for passengers.

classes.label: Airport
classes.definition: An airport.

classes.label: AlignmentObject
classes.definition: An intangible item that describes an alignment between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework. Should not be used where the nature of the alignment can be described using a simple property, for example to express that a resource [[teaches]] or [[assesses]] a competency.

classes.label: AllocateAction
classes.definition: The act of organizing tasks/objects/events by associating resources to it.

classes.label: AmpStory
classes.definition: A creative work with a visual storytelling format intended to be viewed online, particularly on mobile devices.

classes.label: AmusementPark
classes.definition: An amusement park.

classes.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
classes.definition: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a [[NewsArticle]] that, while based on factual reporting, incorporates the expertise of the author/producer, offering interpretations and conclusions.

classes.label: AnatomicalStructure
classes.definition: Any part of the human body, typically a component of an anatomical system. Organs, tissues, and cells are all anatomical structures.

classes.label: AnatomicalSystem
classes.definition: An anatomical system is a group of anatomical structures that work together to perform a certain task. Anatomical systems, such as organ systems, are one organizing principle of anatomy, and can include circulatory, digestive, endocrine, integumentary, immune, lymphatic, muscular, nervous, reproductive, respiratory, skeletal, urinary, vestibular, and other systems.

classes.label: AnimalShelter
classes.definition: Animal shelter.

classes.label: Answer
classes.definition: An answer offered to a question; perhaps correct, perhaps opinionated or wrong.

classes.label: Apartment
classes.definition: An apartment (in American English) or flat (in British English) is a self-contained housing unit (a type of residential real estate) that occupies only part of a building (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartment).

classes.label: ApartmentComplex
classes.definition: Residence type: Apartment complex.

classes.label: AppendAction
classes.definition: The act of inserting at the end if an ordered collection.

classes.label: ApplyAction
classes.definition:
The act of registering to an organization/service without the guarantee to receive it.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, ApplyAction has no guarantees that the application will be accepted.

classes.label: ApprovedIndication
classes.definition: An indication for a medical therapy that has been formally specified or approved by a regulatory body that regulates use of the therapy; for example, the US FDA approves indications for most drugs in the US.

classes.label: Aquarium
classes.definition: Aquarium.

classes.label: ArchiveComponent
classes.definition: An intangible type to be applied to any archive content, carrying with it a set of properties required to describe archival items and collections.

classes.label: ArchiveOrganization
classes.definition: An organization with archival holdings. An organization which keeps and preserves archival material and typically makes it accessible to the public.

classes.label: ArriveAction
classes.definition: The act of arriving at a place. An agent arrives at a destination from a fromLocation, optionally with participants.

classes.label: ArtGallery
classes.definition: An art gallery.

classes.label: Artery
classes.definition: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries blood away from the heart.

classes.label: Article
classes.definition: An article, such as a news article or piece of investigative report. Newspapers and magazines have articles of many different types and this is intended to cover them all.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

classes.label: AskAction
classes.definition:
The act of posing a question / favor to someone.

Related actions:

* [[ReplyAction]]: Appears generally as a response to AskAction.

classes.label: AskPublicNewsArticle
classes.definition: A [[NewsArticle]] expressing an open call by a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] asking the public for input, insights, clarifications, anecdotes, documentation, etc., on an issue, for reporting purposes.

classes.label: AssessAction
classes.definition: The act of forming one's opinion, reaction or sentiment.

classes.label: AssignAction
classes.definition: The act of allocating an action/event/task to some destination (someone or something).

classes.label: Atlas
classes.definition: A collection or bound volume of maps, charts, plates or tables, physical or in media form illustrating any subject.

classes.label: Attorney
classes.definition: Professional service: Attorney. \n\nThis type is deprecated - [[LegalService]] is more inclusive and less ambiguous.

classes.label: Audience
classes.definition: Intended audience for an item, i.e. the group for whom the item was created.

classes.label: AudioObject
classes.definition: An audio file.

classes.label: AudioObjectSnapshot
classes.definition: A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[AudioObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

classes.label: Audiobook
classes.definition: An audiobook.

classes.label: AuthenticateAction
classes.definition: The action of authenticating into a device or application.

classes.label: AuthorizeAction
classes.definition: The act of granting permission to an object.

classes.label: AutoBodyShop
classes.definition: Auto body shop.

classes.label: AutoDealer
classes.definition: An car dealership.

classes.label: AutoPartsStore
classes.definition: An auto parts store.

classes.label: AutoRental
classes.definition: A car rental business.

classes.label: AutoRepair
classes.definition: Car repair business.

classes.label: AutoWash
classes.definition: A car wash business.

classes.label: AutomatedTeller
classes.definition: ATM/cash machine.

classes.label: AutomotiveBusiness
classes.definition: Car repair, sales, or parts.

classes.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
classes.definition: A [[NewsArticle]] providing historical context, definition and detail on a specific topic (aka "explainer" or "backgrounder"). For example, an in-depth article or frequently-asked-questions ([FAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAQ)) document on topics such as Climate Change or the European Union. Other kinds of background material from a non-news setting are often described using [[Book]] or [[Article]], in particular [[ScholarlyArticle]]. See also [[NewsArticle]] for related vocabulary from a learning/education perspective.

classes.label: Bakery
classes.definition: A bakery.

classes.label: BankAccount
classes.definition: A product or service offered by a bank whereby one may deposit, withdraw or transfer money and in some cases be paid interest.

classes.label: BankOrCreditUnion
classes.definition: Bank or credit union.

classes.label: BarOrPub
classes.definition: A bar or pub.

classes.label: Barcode
classes.definition: An image of a visual machine-readable code such as a barcode or QR code.

classes.label: Beach
classes.definition: Beach.

classes.label: BeautySalon
classes.definition: Beauty salon.

classes.label: BedAndBreakfast
classes.definition:
Bed and breakfast.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: BedDetails
classes.definition: An entity holding detailed information about the available bed types, e.g. the quantity of twin beds for a hotel room. For the single case of just one bed of a certain type, you can use bed directly with a text. See also [[BedType]] (under development).

classes.label: BedType
classes.definition: A type of bed. This is used for indicating the bed or beds available in an accommodation.

classes.label: BefriendAction
classes.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone (object) mutually/bidirectionally/symmetrically.

Related actions:

* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, BefriendAction implies that the connection is reciprocal.

classes.label: BikeStore
classes.definition: A bike store.

classes.label: BioChemEntity
classes.definition: Any biological, chemical, or biochemical thing. For example: a protein; a gene; a chemical; a synthetic chemical.

classes.label: Blog
classes.definition: A [blog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog), sometimes known as a "weblog". Note that the individual posts ([[BlogPosting]]s) in a [[Blog]] are often colloquially referred to by the same term.

classes.label: BlogPosting
classes.definition: A blog post.

classes.label: BloodTest
classes.definition: A medical test performed on a sample of a patient's blood.

classes.label: BoardingPolicyType
classes.definition: A type of boarding policy used by an airline.

classes.label: BoatReservation
classes.definition: A reservation for boat travel. Note: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

classes.label: BoatTerminal
classes.definition: A terminal for boats, ships, and other water vessels.

classes.label: BoatTrip
classes.definition: A trip on a commercial ferry line.

classes.label: BodyMeasurementTypeEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates types (or dimensions) of a person's body measurements, for example for fitting of clothes.

classes.label: BodyOfWater
classes.definition: A body of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake.

classes.label: Bone
classes.definition: Rigid connective tissue that comprises up the skeletal structure of the human body.

classes.label: Book
classes.definition: A book.

classes.label: BookFormatType
classes.definition: The publication format of the book.

classes.label: BookSeries
classes.definition: A series of books. Included books can be indicated with the hasPart property.

classes.label: BookStore
classes.definition: A bookstore.

classes.label: BookmarkAction
classes.definition: An agent bookmarks/flags/labels/tags/marks an object.

classes.label: Boolean
classes.definition: Boolean: True or False.

classes.label: BorrowAction
classes.definition:
The act of obtaining an object under an agreement to return it at a later date. Reciprocal of LendAction.

Related actions:

* [[LendAction]]: Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

classes.label: BowlingAlley
classes.definition: A bowling alley.

classes.label: BrainStructure
classes.definition: Any anatomical structure which pertains to the soft nervous tissue functioning as the coordinating center of sensation and intellectual and nervous activity.

classes.label: Brand
classes.definition: A brand is a name used by an organization or business person for labeling a product, product group, or similar.

classes.label: BreadcrumbList
classes.definition: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList consisting of a chain of linked Web pages, typically described using at least their URL and their name, and typically ending with the current page.\n\nThe [[position]] property is used to reconstruct the order of the items in a BreadcrumbList. The convention is that a breadcrumb list has an [[itemListOrder]] of [[ItemListOrderAscending]] (lower values listed first), and that the first items in this list correspond to the "top" or beginning of the breadcrumb trail, e.g. with a site or section homepage. The specific values of 'position' are not assigned meaning for a BreadcrumbList, but they should be integers, e.g. beginning with '1' for the first item in the list.

classes.label: Brewery
classes.definition: Brewery.

classes.label: Bridge
classes.definition: A bridge.

classes.label: BroadcastChannel
classes.definition: A unique instance of a BroadcastService on a CableOrSatelliteService lineup.

classes.label: BroadcastEvent
classes.definition: An over the air or online broadcast event.

classes.label: BroadcastFrequencySpecification
classes.definition: The frequency in MHz and the modulation used for a particular BroadcastService.

classes.label: BroadcastService
classes.definition: A delivery service through which content is provided via broadcast over the air or online.

classes.label: BrokerageAccount
classes.definition: An account that allows an investor to deposit funds and place investment orders with a licensed broker or brokerage firm.

classes.label: BuddhistTemple
classes.definition: A Buddhist temple.

classes.label: BusOrCoach
classes.definition: A bus (also omnibus or autobus) is a road vehicle designed to carry passengers. Coaches are luxury buses, usually in service for long distance travel.

classes.label: BusReservation
classes.definition: A reservation for bus travel. \n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

classes.label: BusStation
classes.definition: A bus station.

classes.label: BusStop
classes.definition: A bus stop.

classes.label: BusTrip
classes.definition: A trip on a commercial bus line.

classes.label: BusinessAudience
classes.definition: A set of characteristics belonging to businesses, e.g. who compose an item's target audience.

classes.label: BusinessEntityType
classes.definition:
A business entity type is a conceptual entity representing the legal form, the size, the main line of business, the position in the value chain, or any combination thereof, of an organization or business person.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Business
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Enduser
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PublicInstitution
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Reseller

classes.label: BusinessEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Business event.

classes.label: BusinessFunction
classes.definition:
The business function specifies the type of activity or access (i.e., the bundle of rights) offered by the organization or business person through the offer. Typical are sell, rental or lease, maintenance or repair, manufacture / produce, recycle / dispose, engineering / construction, or installation. Proprietary specifications of access rights are also instances of this class.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ConstructionInstallation
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Dispose
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Maintain
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ProvideService
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Repair
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Buy

classes.label: BuyAction
classes.definition: The act of giving money to a seller in exchange for goods or services rendered. An agent buys an object, product, or service from a seller for a price. Reciprocal of SellAction.

classes.label: CDCPMDRecord
classes.definition: A CDCPMDRecord is a data structure representing a record in a CDC tabular data format used for hospital data reporting. See [documentation](/docs/cdc-covid.html) for details, and the linked CDC materials for authoritative definitions used as the source here.

classes.label: CableOrSatelliteService
classes.definition: A service which provides access to media programming like TV or radio. Access may be via cable or satellite.

classes.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
classes.definition: A cafe or coffee shop.

classes.label: Campground
classes.definition:
A camping site, campsite, or [[Campground]] is a place used for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically containing individual [[CampingPitch]] locations. 

 In British English a campsite is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or park a camper; a campground may contain many campsites (source: Wikipedia, see [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite)).

 See also the dedicated [document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations](/docs/hotels.html).

classes.label: CampingPitch
classes.definition:
A [[CampingPitch]] is an individual place for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically being part of a larger camping site, or [[Campground]].

 In British English a campsite, or campground, is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or park a camper; a campground may contain many campsites. (Source: Wikipedia, see [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite).)

 See also the dedicated [document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations](/docs/hotels.html).

classes.label: Canal
classes.definition: A canal, like the Panama Canal.

classes.label: CancelAction
classes.definition:
The act of asserting that a future event/action is no longer going to happen.

Related actions:

* [[ConfirmAction]]: The antonym of CancelAction.

classes.label: Car
classes.definition: A car is a wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle used for transportation.

classes.label: CarUsageType
classes.definition: A value indicating a special usage of a car, e.g. commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi.

classes.label: Casino
classes.definition: A casino.

classes.label: CategoryCode
classes.definition: A Category Code.

classes.label: CategoryCodeSet
classes.definition: A set of Category Code values.

classes.label: CatholicChurch
classes.definition: A Catholic church.

classes.label: Cemetery
classes.definition: A graveyard.

classes.label: Certification
classes.definition: A Certification is an official and authoritative statement about a subject, for example a product, service, person, or organization. A certification is typically issued by an indendent certification body, for example a professional organization or government. It formally attests certain characteristics about the subject, for example Organizations can be ISO certified, Food products can be certified Organic or Vegan, a Person can be a certified professional, a Place can be certified for food processing. There are certifications for many domains: regulatory, organizational, recycling, food, efficiency, educational, ecological, etc. A certification is a form of credential, as are accreditations and licenses. Mapped from the [gs1:CertificationDetails](https://www.gs1.org/voc/CertificationDetails) class in the GS1 Web Vocabulary.

classes.label: CertificationStatusEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates the different statuses of a Certification (Active and Inactive).

classes.label: Chapter
classes.definition: One of the sections into which a book is divided. A chapter usually has a section number or a name.

classes.label: CheckAction
classes.definition: An agent inspects, determines, investigates, inquires, or examines an object's accuracy, quality, condition, or state.

classes.label: CheckInAction
classes.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their arrival by registering/confirming for a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check-in) or at a place (e.g. hotel), possibly resulting in a result (boarding pass, etc).

Related actions:

* [[CheckOutAction]]: The antonym of CheckInAction.
* [[ArriveAction]]: Unlike ArriveAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service.
* [[ConfirmAction]]: Unlike ConfirmAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the *start* of a previously reserved service rather than its validity/existence.

classes.label: CheckOutAction
classes.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their departure of a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check-in) or place (e.g. hotel).

Related actions:

* [[CheckInAction]]: The antonym of CheckOutAction.
* [[DepartAction]]: Unlike DepartAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.
* [[CancelAction]]: Unlike CancelAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.

classes.label: CheckoutPage
classes.definition: Web page type: Checkout page.

classes.label: ChemicalSubstance
classes.definition: A chemical substance is 'a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types' (source: [ChEBI:59999](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=59999)).

classes.label: ChildCare
classes.definition: A Childcare center.

classes.label: ChildrensEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Children's event.

classes.label: ChooseAction
classes.definition: The act of expressing a preference from a set of options or a large or unbounded set of choices/options.

classes.label: Church
classes.definition: A church.

classes.label: City
classes.definition: A city or town.

classes.label: CityHall
classes.definition: A city hall.

classes.label: CivicStructure
classes.definition: A public structure, such as a town hall or concert hall.

classes.label: Claim
classes.definition: A [[Claim]] in Schema.org represents a specific, factually-oriented claim that could be the [[itemReviewed]] in a [[ClaimReview]]. The content of a claim can be summarized with the [[text]] property. Variations on well known claims can have their common identity indicated via [[sameAs]] links, and summarized with a [[name]]. Ideally, a [[Claim]] description includes enough contextual information to minimize the risk of ambiguity or inclarity. In practice, many claims are better understood in the context in which they appear or the interpretations provided by claim reviews. Beyond [[ClaimReview]], the Claim type can be associated with related creative works - for example a [[ScholarlyArticle]] or [[Question]] might be [[about]] some [[Claim]]. At this time, Schema.org does not define any types of relationship between claims. This is a natural area for future exploration.

classes.label: ClaimReview
classes.definition: A fact-checking review of claims made (or reported) in some creative work (referenced via itemReviewed).

classes.label: Class
classes.definition: A class, also often called a 'Type'; equivalent to rdfs:Class.

classes.label: Clip
classes.definition: A short TV or radio program or a segment/part of a program.

classes.label: ClothingStore
classes.definition: A clothing store.

classes.label: Code
classes.definition: Computer programming source code. Example: Full (compile ready) solutions, code snippet samples, scripts, templates.

classes.label: Collection
classes.definition: A collection of items, e.g. creative works or products.

classes.label: CollectionPage
classes.definition: Web page type: Collection page.

classes.label: CollegeOrUniversity
classes.definition: A college, university, or other third-level educational institution.

classes.label: ComedyClub
classes.definition: A comedy club.

classes.label: ComedyEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Comedy event.

classes.label: ComicCoverArt
classes.definition: The artwork on the cover of a comic.

classes.label: ComicIssue
classes.definition: Individual comic issues are serially published as part of a larger series. For the sake of consistency, even one-shot issues belong to a series comprised of a single issue. All comic issues can be uniquely identified by: the combination of the name and volume number of the series to which the issue belongs; the issue number; and the variant description of the issue (if any).

classes.label: ComicSeries
classes.definition: A sequential publication of comic stories under a unifying title, for example "The Amazing Spider-Man" or "Groo the Wanderer".

classes.label: ComicStory
classes.definition: The term "story" is any indivisible, re-printable unit of a comic, including the interior stories, covers, and backmatter. Most comics have at least two stories: a cover (ComicCoverArt) and an interior story.

classes.label: Comment
classes.definition: A comment on an item - for example, a comment on a blog post. The comment's content is expressed via the [[text]] property, and its topic via [[about]], properties shared with all CreativeWorks.

classes.label: CommentAction
classes.definition: The act of generating a comment about a subject.

classes.label: CommunicateAction
classes.definition: The act of conveying information to another person via a communication medium (instrument) such as speech, email, or telephone conversation.

classes.label: CompleteDataFeed
classes.definition: A [[CompleteDataFeed]] is a [[DataFeed]] whose standard representation includes content for every item currently in the feed. This is the equivalent of Atom's element as defined in Feed Paging and Archiving [RFC 5005](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5005), for example (and as defined for Atom), when using data from a feed that represents a collection of items that varies over time (e.g. "Top Twenty Records") there is no need to have newer entries mixed in alongside older, obsolete entries. By marking this feed as a CompleteDataFeed, old entries can be safely discarded when the feed is refreshed, since we can assume the feed has provided descriptions for all current items.

classes.label: CompoundPriceSpecification
classes.definition: A compound price specification is one that bundles multiple prices that all apply in combination for different dimensions of consumption. Use the name property of the attached unit price specification for indicating the dimension of a price component (e.g. "electricity" or "final cleaning").

classes.label: ComputerLanguage
classes.definition: This type covers computer programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, as well as other language-like computer representations. Natural languages are best represented with the [[Language]] type.

classes.label: ComputerStore
classes.definition: A computer store.

classes.label: ConferenceEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Conference event.

classes.label: ConfirmAction
classes.definition:
The act of notifying someone that a future event/action is going to happen as expected.

Related actions:

* [[CancelAction]]: The antonym of ConfirmAction.

classes.label: Consortium
classes.definition: A Consortium is a membership [[Organization]] whose members are typically Organizations.

classes.label: ConstraintNode
classes.definition: The ConstraintNode type is provided to support usecases in which a node in a structured data graph is described with properties which appear to describe a single entity, but are being used in a situation where they serve a more abstract purpose. A [[ConstraintNode]] can be described using [[constraintProperty]] and [[numConstraints]]. These constraint properties can serve a variety of purposes, and their values may sometimes be understood to indicate sets of possible values rather than single, exact and specific values.

classes.label: ConsumeAction
classes.definition: The act of ingesting information/resources/food.

classes.label: ContactPage
classes.definition: Web page type: Contact page.

classes.label: ContactPoint
classes.definition: A contact point—for example, a Customer Complaints department.

classes.label: ContactPointOption
classes.definition: Enumerated options related to a ContactPoint.

classes.label: Continent
classes.definition: One of the continents (for example, Europe or Africa).

classes.label: ControlAction
classes.definition: An agent controls a device or application.

classes.label: ConvenienceStore
classes.definition: A convenience store.

classes.label: Conversation
classes.definition: One or more messages between organizations or people on a particular topic. Individual messages can be linked to the conversation with isPartOf or hasPart properties.

classes.label: CookAction
classes.definition: The act of producing/preparing food.

classes.label: Cooperative
classes.definition: An organization that is a joint project of multiple organizations or persons.

classes.label: Corporation
classes.definition: Organization: A business corporation.

classes.label: CorrectionComment
classes.definition: A [[comment]] that corrects [[CreativeWork]].

classes.label: Country
classes.definition: A country.

classes.label: Course
classes.definition: A description of an educational course which may be offered as distinct instances which take place at different times or take place at different locations, or be offered through different media or modes of study. An educational course is a sequence of one or more educational events and/or creative works which aims to build knowledge, competence or ability of learners.

classes.label: CourseInstance
classes.definition: An instance of a [[Course]] which is distinct from other instances because it is offered at a different time or location or through different media or modes of study or to a specific section of students.

classes.label: Courthouse
classes.definition: A courthouse.

classes.label: CoverArt
classes.definition: The artwork on the outer surface of a CreativeWork.

classes.label: CovidTestingFacility
classes.definition: A CovidTestingFacility is a [[MedicalClinic]] where testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease is available. If the facility is being made available from an established [[Pharmacy]], [[Hotel]], or other non-medical organization, multiple types can be listed. This makes it easier to re-use existing schema.org information about that place, e.g. contact info, address, opening hours. Note that in an emergency, such information may not always be reliable.

classes.label: CreateAction
classes.definition: The act of deliberately creating/producing/generating/building a result out of the agent.

classes.label: CreativeWork
classes.definition: The most generic kind of creative work, including books, movies, photographs, software programs, etc.

classes.label: CreativeWorkSeason
classes.definition: A media season, e.g. TV, radio, video game etc.

classes.label: CreativeWorkSeries
classes.definition:
A CreativeWorkSeries in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. CreativeWorkSeries are usually organized into some order, often chronological. Unlike [[ItemList]] which is a general purpose data structure for lists of things, the emphasis with CreativeWorkSeries is on published materials (written e.g. books and periodicals, or media such as TV, radio and games).

Specific subtypes are available for describing [[TVSeries]], [[RadioSeries]], [[MovieSeries]], [[BookSeries]], [[Periodical]] and [[VideoGameSeries]]. In each case, the [[hasPart]] / [[isPartOf]] properties can be used to relate the CreativeWorkSeries to its parts. The general CreativeWorkSeries type serves largely just to organize these more specific and practical subtypes.

It is common for properties applicable to an item from the series to be usefully applied to the containing group. Schema.org attempts to anticipate some of these cases, but publishers should be free to apply properties of the series parts to the series as a whole wherever they seem appropriate.

classes.label: Credential
classes.definition: A credential is a certificate that is used to verify the identity of a person or entity.

classes.label: CreditCard
classes.definition:
A card payment method of a particular brand or name. Used to mark up a particular payment method and/or the financial product/service that supplies the card account.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#AmericanExpress
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DinersClub
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Discover
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#JCB
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#MasterCard
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#VISA

classes.label: Crematorium
classes.definition: A crematorium.

classes.label: CriticReview
classes.definition: A [[CriticReview]] is a more specialized form of Review written or published by a source that is recognized for its reviewing activities. These can include online columns, travel and food guides, TV and radio shows, blogs and other independent Web sites. [[CriticReview]]s are typically more in-depth and professionally written. For simpler, casually written user/visitor/viewer/customer reviews, it is more appropriate to use the [[UserReview]] type. Review aggregator sites such as Metacritic already separate out the site's user reviews from selected critic reviews that originate from third-party sources.

classes.label: CssSelectorType
classes.definition: Text representing a CSS selector.

classes.label: CurrencyConversionService
classes.definition: A service to convert funds from one currency to another currency.

classes.label: DDxElement
classes.definition: An alternative, closely-related condition typically considered later in the differential diagnosis process along with the signs that are used to distinguish it.

classes.label: DENonprofitType
classes.definition: DENonprofitType: Non-profit organization type originating from Germany in accordance with article 52 of the German fiscal code (Abgabenverordnung or AO).

classes.label: DanceEvent
classes.definition: Event type: A social dance.

classes.label: DanceGroup
classes.definition: A dance group—for example, the Alvin Ailey Dance Theater or Riverdance.

classes.label: DataCatalog
classes.definition: A collection of datasets.

classes.label: DataDownload
classes.definition: All or part of a [[Dataset]] in downloadable form.

classes.label: DataFeed
classes.definition: A single feed providing structured information about one or more entities or topics.

classes.label: DataFeedItem
classes.definition: A single item within a larger data feed.

classes.label: DataType
classes.definition: The basic data types such as Integers, Strings, etc.

classes.label: Dataset
classes.definition: A body of structured information describing some topic(s) of interest.

classes.label: Date
classes.definition: A date value in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).

classes.label: DateTime
classes.definition: A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see Chapter 5.4 of ISO 8601).

classes.label: DatedMoneySpecification
classes.definition: A DatedMoneySpecification represents monetary values with optional start and end dates. For example, this could represent an employee's salary over a specific period of time. __Note:__ This type has been superseded by [[MonetaryAmount]], use of that type is recommended.

classes.label: DayOfWeek
classes.definition: The day of the week, e.g. used to specify to which day the opening hours of an OpeningHoursSpecification refer. Originally, URLs from [GoodRelations](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1) were used (for [[Monday]], [[Tuesday]], [[Wednesday]], [[Thursday]], [[Friday]], [[Saturday]], [[Sunday]] plus a special entry for [[PublicHolidays]]); these have now been integrated directly into schema.org.

classes.label: DaySpa
classes.definition: A day spa.

classes.label: DeactivateAction
classes.definition: The act of stopping or deactivating a device or application (e.g. stopping a timer or turning off a flashlight).

classes.label: DefenceEstablishment
classes.definition: A defence establishment, such as an army or navy base.

classes.label: DefinedRegion
classes.definition: A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes. Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured. Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA" Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Region = state, canton, prefecture, autonomous community...

classes.label: DefinedTerm
classes.definition: A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what the term is about.

classes.label: DefinedTermSet
classes.definition: A set of defined terms, for example a set of categories or a classification scheme, a glossary, dictionary or enumeration. Use the about property to specify what the term set is about.

classes.label: DeleteAction
classes.definition: The act of editing a recipient by removing one of its objects.

classes.label: DeliveryChargeSpecification
classes.definition: The price for the delivery of an offer using a particular delivery method.

classes.label: DeliveryEvent
classes.definition: An event involving the delivery of an item.

classes.label: DeliveryMethod
classes.definition:
A delivery method is a standardized procedure for transferring the product or service to the destination of fulfillment chosen by the customer. Delivery methods are characterized by the means of transportation used, and by the organization or group that is the contracting party for the sending organization or person.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeDirectDownload
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeFreight
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeMail
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeOwnFleet
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModePickUp
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#UPS

classes.label: Demand
classes.definition: A demand entity represents the public, not necessarily binding, not necessarily exclusive, announcement by an organization or person to seek a certain type of goods or services. For describing demand using this type, the very same properties used for Offer apply.

classes.label: Dentist
classes.definition: A dentist.

classes.label: DepartAction
classes.definition: The act of departing from a place. An agent departs from a fromLocation for a destination, optionally with participants.

classes.label: DepartmentStore
classes.definition: A department store.

classes.label: DepositAccount
classes.definition: A type of Bank Account with a main purpose of depositing funds to gain interest or other benefits.

classes.label: DiagnosticLab
classes.definition: A medical laboratory that offers on-site or off-site diagnostic services.

classes.label: DiagnosticProcedure
classes.definition: A medical procedure intended primarily for diagnostic, as opposed to therapeutic, purposes.

classes.label: Diet
classes.definition: A strategy of regulating the intake of food to achieve or maintain a specific health-related goal.

classes.label: DietarySupplement
classes.definition: A product taken by mouth that contains a dietary ingredient intended to supplement the diet. Dietary ingredients may include vitamins, minerals, herbs or other botanicals, amino acids, and substances such as enzymes, organ tissues, glandulars and metabolites.

classes.label: DigitalDocument
classes.definition: An electronic file or document.

classes.label: DigitalDocumentPermission
classes.definition: A permission for a particular person or group to access a particular file.

classes.label: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
classes.definition: A type of permission which can be granted for accessing a digital document.

classes.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates some common technology platforms, for use with properties such as [[actionPlatform]]. It is not supposed to be comprehensive - when a suitable code is not enumerated here, textual or URL values can be used instead. These codes are at a fairly high level and do not deal with versioning and other nuance. Additional codes can be suggested [in github](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/3057).

classes.label: DisagreeAction
classes.definition: The act of expressing a difference of opinion with the object. An agent disagrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

classes.label: DiscoverAction
classes.definition: The act of discovering/finding an object.

classes.label: DiscussionForumPosting
classes.definition: A posting to a discussion forum.

classes.label: DislikeAction
classes.definition: The act of expressing a negative sentiment about the object. An agent dislikes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

classes.label: Distance
classes.definition: Properties that take Distances as values are of the form '<Number> <Length unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 ft'.

classes.label: Distillery
classes.definition: A distillery.

classes.label: DonateAction
classes.definition: The act of providing goods, services, or money without compensation, often for philanthropic reasons.

classes.label: DoseSchedule
classes.definition: A specific dosing schedule for a drug or supplement.

classes.label: DownloadAction
classes.definition: The act of downloading an object.

classes.label: DrawAction
classes.definition: The act of producing a visual/graphical representation of an object, typically with a pen/pencil and paper as instruments.

classes.label: Drawing
classes.definition: A picture or diagram made with a pencil, pen, or crayon rather than paint.

classes.label: DrinkAction
classes.definition: The act of swallowing liquids.

classes.label: DriveWheelConfigurationValue
classes.definition: A value indicating which roadwheels will receive torque.

classes.label: Drug
classes.definition: A chemical or biologic substance, used as a medical therapy, that has a physiological effect on an organism. Here the term drug is used interchangeably with the term medicine although clinical knowledge makes a clear difference between them.

classes.label: DrugClass
classes.definition: A class of medical drugs, e.g., statins. Classes can represent general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, common physiological effects, etc.

classes.label: DrugCost
classes.definition: The cost per unit of a medical drug. Note that this type is not meant to represent the price in an offer of a drug for sale; see the Offer type for that. This type will typically be used to tag wholesale or average retail cost of a drug, or maximum reimbursable cost. Costs of medical drugs vary widely depending on how and where they are paid for, so while this type captures some of the variables, costs should be used with caution by consumers of this schema's markup.

classes.label: DrugCostCategory
classes.definition: Enumerated categories of medical drug costs.

classes.label: DrugLegalStatus
classes.definition: The legal availability status of a medical drug.

classes.label: DrugPregnancyCategory
classes.definition: Categories that represent an assessment of the risk of fetal injury due to a drug or pharmaceutical used as directed by the mother during pregnancy.

classes.label: DrugPrescriptionStatus
classes.definition: Indicates whether this drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter.

classes.label: DrugStrength
classes.definition: A specific strength in which a medical drug is available in a specific country.

classes.label: DryCleaningOrLaundry
classes.definition: A dry-cleaning business.

classes.label: Duration
classes.definition: Quantity: Duration (use [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).

classes.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates the EU energy efficiency classes A-G as well as A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369.

classes.label: EatAction
classes.definition: The act of swallowing solid objects.

classes.label: EducationEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Education event.

classes.label: EducationalAudience
classes.definition: An EducationalAudience.

classes.label: EducationalOccupationalCredential
classes.definition: An educational or occupational credential. A diploma, academic degree, certification, qualification, badge, etc., that may be awarded to a person or other entity that meets the requirements defined by the credentialer.

classes.label: EducationalOccupationalProgram
classes.definition: A program offered by an institution which determines the learning progress to achieve an outcome, usually a credential like a degree or certificate. This would define a discrete set of opportunities (e.g., job, courses) that together constitute a program with a clear start, end, set of requirements, and transition to a new occupational opportunity (e.g., a job), or sometimes a higher educational opportunity (e.g., an advanced degree).

classes.label: EducationalOrganization
classes.definition: An educational organization.

classes.label: Electrician
classes.definition: An electrician.

classes.label: ElectronicsStore
classes.definition: An electronics store.

classes.label: ElementarySchool
classes.definition: An elementary school.

classes.label: EmailMessage
classes.definition: An email message.

classes.label: Embassy
classes.definition: An embassy.

classes.label: EmergencyService
classes.definition: An emergency service, such as a fire station or ER.

classes.label: EmployeeRole
classes.definition: A subclass of OrganizationRole used to describe employee relationships.

classes.label: EmployerAggregateRating
classes.definition: An aggregate rating of an Organization related to its role as an employer.

classes.label: EmployerReview
classes.definition: An [[EmployerReview]] is a review of an [[Organization]] regarding its role as an employer, written by a current or former employee of that organization.

classes.label: EmploymentAgency
classes.definition: An employment agency.

classes.label: EndorseAction
classes.definition: An agent approves/certifies/likes/supports/sanctions an object.

classes.label: EndorsementRating
classes.definition: An EndorsementRating is a rating that expresses some level of endorsement, for example inclusion in a "critic's pick" blog, a "Like" or "+1" on a social network. It can be considered the [[result]] of an [[EndorseAction]] in which the [[object]] of the action is rated positively by some [[agent]]. As is common elsewhere in schema.org, it is sometimes more useful to describe the results of such an action without explicitly describing the [[Action]]. An [[EndorsementRating]] may be part of a numeric scale or organized system, but this is not required: having an explicit type for indicating a positive, endorsement rating is particularly useful in the absence of numeric scales as it helps consumers understand that the rating is broadly positive.

classes.label: Energy
classes.definition: Properties that take Energy as values are of the form '<Number> <Energy unit of measure>'.

classes.label: EnergyConsumptionDetails
classes.definition: EnergyConsumptionDetails represents information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy. The information that can be provided is based on international regulations such as for example [EU directive 2017/1369](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/1369/oj) for energy labeling and the [Energy labeling rule](https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/rules/rulemaking-regulatory-reform-proceedings/energy-water-use-labeling-consumer) under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) in the US.

classes.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates energy efficiency levels (also known as "classes" or "ratings") and certifications that are part of several international energy efficiency standards.

classes.label: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
classes.definition: Used to indicate whether a product is EnergyStar certified.

classes.label: EngineSpecification
classes.definition: Information about the engine of the vehicle. A vehicle can have multiple engines represented by multiple engine specification entities.

classes.label: EntertainmentBusiness
classes.definition: A business providing entertainment.

classes.label: EntryPoint
classes.definition: An entry point, within some Web-based protocol.

classes.label: Enumeration
classes.definition: Lists or enumerations—for example, a list of cuisines or music genres, etc.

classes.label: Episode
classes.definition: A media episode (e.g. TV, radio, video game) which can be part of a series or season.

classes.label: Error
classes.definition: Representation of an Error.

classes.label: Event
classes.definition: An event happening at a certain time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Ticketing information may be added via the [[offers]] property. Repeated events may be structured as separate Event objects.

classes.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
classes.definition: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration value is one of potentially several modes of organising an event, relating to whether it is online or offline.

classes.label: EventReservation
classes.definition: A reservation for an event like a concert, sporting event, or lecture.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

classes.label: EventSeries
classes.definition: A series of [[Event]]s. Included events can relate with the series using the [[superEvent]] property. An EventSeries is a collection of events that share some unifying characteristic. For example, "The Olympic Games" is a series, which is repeated regularly. The "2012 London Olympics" can be presented both as an [[Event]] in the series "Olympic Games", and as an [[EventSeries]] that included a number of sporting competitions as Events. The nature of the association between the events in an [[EventSeries]] can vary, but typical examples could include a thematic event series (e.g. topical meetups or classes), or a series of regular events that share a location, attendee group and/or organizers. EventSeries has been defined as a kind of Event to make it easy for publishers to use it in an Event context without worrying about which kinds of series are really event-like enough to call an Event. In general an EventSeries may seem more Event-like when the period of time is compact and when aspects such as location are fixed, but it may also sometimes prove useful to describe a longer-term series as an Event.

classes.label: EventStatusType
classes.definition: EventStatusType is an enumeration type whose instances represent several states that an Event may be in.

classes.label: EventVenue
classes.definition: An event venue.

classes.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
classes.definition: A structured value representing exchange rate.

classes.label: ExerciseAction
classes.definition: The act of participating in exertive activity for the purposes of improving health and fitness.

classes.label: ExerciseGym
classes.definition: A gym.

classes.label: ExercisePlan
classes.definition: Fitness-related activity designed for a specific health-related purpose, including defined exercise routines as well as activity prescribed by a clinician.

classes.label: ExhibitionEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Exhibition event, e.g. at a museum, library, archive, tradeshow, ...

classes.label: FAQPage
classes.definition: A [[FAQPage]] is a [[WebPage]] presenting one or more "[Frequently asked questions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAQ)" (see also [[QAPage]]).

classes.label: FMRadioChannel
classes.definition: A radio channel that uses FM.

classes.label: FastFoodRestaurant
classes.definition: A fast-food restaurant.

classes.label: Festival
classes.definition: Event type: Festival.

classes.label: FilmAction
classes.definition: The act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally.

classes.label: FinancialIncentive
classes.definition:
Represents financial incentives for goods/services offered by an organization (or individual).

Typically contains the [[name]] of the incentive, the [[incentivizedItem]], the [[incentiveAmount]], the [[incentiveStatus]], [[incentiveType]], the [[provider]] of the incentive, and [[eligibleWithSupplier]].

Optionally contains criteria on whether the incentive is limited based on [[purchaseType]], [[purchasePriceLimit]], [[incomeLimit]], and the [[qualifiedExpense]].

classes.label: FinancialProduct
classes.definition: A product provided to consumers and businesses by financial institutions such as banks, insurance companies, brokerage firms, consumer finance companies, and investment companies which comprise the financial services industry.

classes.label: FinancialService
classes.definition: Financial services business.

classes.label: FindAction
classes.definition:
The act of finding an object.

Related actions:

* [[SearchAction]]: FindAction is generally lead by a SearchAction, but not necessarily.

classes.label: FireStation
classes.definition: A fire station. With firemen.

classes.label: Flight
classes.definition: An airline flight.

classes.label: FlightReservation
classes.definition: A reservation for air travel.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

classes.label: Float
classes.definition: Data type: Floating number.

classes.label: FloorPlan
classes.definition: A FloorPlan is an explicit representation of a collection of similar accommodations, allowing the provision of common information (room counts, sizes, layout diagrams) and offers for rental or sale. In typical use, some [[ApartmentComplex]] has an [[accommodationFloorPlan]] which is a [[FloorPlan]]. A FloorPlan is always in the context of a particular place, either a larger [[ApartmentComplex]] or a single [[Apartment]]. The visual/spatial aspects of a floor plan (i.e. room layout, [see wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floor_plan)) can be indicated using [[image]].

classes.label: Florist
classes.definition: A florist.

classes.label: FollowAction
classes.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.

Related actions:

* [[BefriendAction]]: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.
* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.
* [[TrackAction]]: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it).

classes.label: FoodEstablishment
classes.definition: A food-related business.

classes.label: FoodEstablishmentReservation
classes.definition: A reservation to dine at a food-related business.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

classes.label: FoodEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Food event.

classes.label: FoodService
classes.definition: A food service, like breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

classes.label: FulfillmentTypeEnumeration
classes.definition: A type of product fulfillment.

classes.label: FundingAgency
classes.definition: A FundingAgency is an organization that implements one or more [[FundingScheme]]s and manages the granting process (via [[Grant]]s, typically [[MonetaryGrant]]s). A funding agency is not always required for grant funding, e.g. philanthropic giving, corporate sponsorship etc. Examples of funding agencies include ERC, REA, NIH, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, ...

classes.label: FundingScheme
classes.definition: A FundingScheme combines organizational, project and policy aspects of grant-based funding that sets guidelines, principles and mechanisms to support other kinds of projects and activities. Funding is typically organized via [[Grant]] funding. Examples of funding schemes: Swiss Priority Programmes (SPPs); EU Framework 7 (FP7); Horizon 2020; the NIH-R01 Grant Program; Wellcome institutional strategic support fund. For large scale public sector funding, the management and administration of grant awards is often handled by other, dedicated, organizations - [[FundingAgency]]s such as ERC, REA, ...

classes.label: FurnitureStore
classes.definition: A furniture store.

classes.label: Game
classes.definition: The Game type represents things which are games. These are typically rule-governed recreational activities, e.g. role-playing games in which players assume the role of characters in a fictional setting.

classes.label: GameAvailabilityEnumeration
classes.definition: For a [[VideoGame]], such as used with a [[PlayGameAction]], an enumeration of the kind of game availability offered.

classes.label: GamePlayMode
classes.definition: Indicates whether this game is multi-player, co-op or single-player.

classes.label: GameServer
classes.definition: Server that provides game interaction in a multiplayer game.

classes.label: GameServerStatus
classes.definition: Status of a game server.

classes.label: GardenStore
classes.definition: A garden store.

classes.label: GasStation
classes.definition: A gas station.

classes.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
classes.definition: Residence type: Gated community.

classes.label: GenderType
classes.definition: An enumeration of genders.

classes.label: Gene
classes.definition: A discrete unit of inheritance which affects one or more biological traits (Source: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)). Examples include FOXP2 (Forkhead box protein P2), SCARNA21 (small Cajal body-specific RNA 21), A- (agouti genotype).

classes.label: GeneralContractor
classes.definition: A general contractor.

classes.label: GeoCircle
classes.definition: A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area. As it is a GeoShape it provides the simple textual property 'circle', but also allows the combination of postalCode alongside geoRadius. The center of the circle can be indicated via the 'geoMidpoint' property, or more approximately using 'address', 'postalCode'.

classes.label: GeoCoordinates
classes.definition: The geographic coordinates of a place or event.

classes.label: GeoShape
classes.definition: The geographic shape of a place. A GeoShape can be described using several properties whose values are based on latitude/longitude pairs. Either whitespace or commas can be used to separate latitude and longitude; whitespace should be used when writing a list of several such points.

classes.label: GeospatialGeometry
classes.definition: (Eventually to be defined as) a supertype of GeoShape designed to accommodate definitions from Geo-Spatial best practices.

classes.label: GiveAction
classes.definition:
The act of transferring ownership of an object to a destination. Reciprocal of TakeAction.

Related actions:

* [[TakeAction]]: Reciprocal of GiveAction.
* [[SendAction]]: Unlike SendAction, GiveAction implies that ownership is being transferred (e.g. I may send my laptop to you, but that doesn't mean I'm giving it to you).

classes.label: GolfCourse
classes.definition: A golf course.

classes.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
classes.definition: GovernmentBenefitsType enumerates several kinds of government benefits to support the COVID-19 situation. Note that this structure may not capture all benefits offered.

classes.label: GovernmentBuilding
classes.definition: A government building.

classes.label: GovernmentOffice
classes.definition: A government office—for example, an IRS or DMV office.

classes.label: GovernmentOrganization
classes.definition: A governmental organization or agency.

classes.label: GovernmentPermit
classes.definition: A permit issued by a government agency.

classes.label: GovernmentService
classes.definition: A service provided by a government organization, e.g. food stamps, veterans benefits, etc.

classes.label: Grant
classes.definition: A grant, typically financial or otherwise quantifiable, of resources. Typically a [[funder]] sponsors some [[MonetaryAmount]] to an [[Organization]] or [[Person]], sometimes not necessarily via a dedicated or long-lived [[Project]], resulting in one or more outputs, or [[fundedItem]]s. For financial sponsorship, indicate the [[funder]] of a [[MonetaryGrant]]. For non-financial support, indicate [[sponsor]] of [[Grant]]s of resources (e.g. office space). Grants support activities directed towards some agreed collective goals, often but not always organized as [[Project]]s. Long-lived projects are sometimes sponsored by a variety of grants over time, but it is also common for a project to be associated with a single grant. The amount of a [[Grant]] is represented using [[amount]] as a [[MonetaryAmount]].

classes.label: GroceryStore
classes.definition: A grocery store.

classes.label: Guide
classes.definition: [[Guide]] is a page or article that recommends specific products or services, or aspects of a thing for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Buying Guide and detail aspects of products or services for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Product Guide and recommend specific products or services. A [[Guide]] may represent a Ranked List and recommend specific products or services with ranking.

classes.label: HVACBusiness
classes.definition: A business that provides Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning services.

classes.label: Hackathon
classes.definition: A [hackathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackathon) event.

classes.label: HairSalon
classes.definition: A hair salon.

classes.label: HardwareStore
classes.definition: A hardware store.

classes.label: HealthAndBeautyBusiness
classes.definition: Health and beauty.

classes.label: HealthAspectEnumeration
classes.definition: HealthAspectEnumeration enumerates several aspects of health content online, each of which might be described using [[hasHealthAspect]] and [[HealthTopicContent]].

classes.label: HealthClub
classes.definition: A health club.

classes.label: HealthInsurancePlan
classes.definition: A US-style health insurance plan, including PPOs, EPOs, and HMOs.

classes.label: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification
classes.definition: A description of costs to the patient under a given network or formulary.

classes.label: HealthPlanFormulary
classes.definition: For a given health insurance plan, the specification for costs and coverage of prescription drugs.

classes.label: HealthPlanNetwork
classes.definition: A US-style health insurance plan network.

classes.label: HealthTopicContent
classes.definition: [[HealthTopicContent]] is [[WebContent]] that is about some aspect of a health topic, e.g. a condition, its symptoms or treatments. Such content may be comprised of several parts or sections and use different types of media. Multiple instances of [[WebContent]] (and hence [[HealthTopicContent]]) can be related using [[hasPart]] / [[isPartOf]] where there is some kind of content hierarchy, and their content described with [[about]] and [[mentions]] e.g. building upon the existing [[MedicalCondition]] vocabulary.

classes.label: HighSchool
classes.definition: A high school.

classes.label: HinduTemple
classes.definition: A Hindu temple.

classes.label: HobbyShop
classes.definition: A store that sells materials useful or necessary for various hobbies.

classes.label: HomeAndConstructionBusiness
classes.definition:
A construction business.

A HomeAndConstructionBusiness is a [[LocalBusiness]] that provides services around homes and buildings.

As a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

classes.label: HomeGoodsStore
classes.definition: A home goods store.

classes.label: Hospital
classes.definition: A hospital.

classes.label: Hostel
classes.definition:
A hostel - cheap accommodation, often in shared dormitories.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: Hotel
classes.definition:
A hotel is an establishment that provides lodging paid on a short-term basis (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: HotelRoom
classes.definition:
A hotel room is a single room in a hotel.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: House
classes.definition: A house is a building or structure that has the ability to be occupied for habitation by humans or other creatures (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House).

classes.label: HousePainter
classes.definition: A house painting service.

classes.label: HowTo
classes.definition: Instructions that explain how to achieve a result by performing a sequence of steps.

classes.label: HowToDirection
classes.definition: A direction indicating a single action to do in the instructions for how to achieve a result.

classes.label: HowToItem
classes.definition: An item used as either a tool or supply when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result.

classes.label: HowToSection
classes.definition: A sub-grouping of steps in the instructions for how to achieve a result (e.g. steps for making a pie crust within a pie recipe).

classes.label: HowToStep
classes.definition: A step in the instructions for how to achieve a result. It is an ordered list with HowToDirection and/or HowToTip items.

classes.label: HowToSupply
classes.definition: A supply consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result.

classes.label: HowToTip
classes.definition: An explanation in the instructions for how to achieve a result. It provides supplementary information about a technique, supply, author's preference, etc. It can explain what could be done, or what should not be done, but doesn't specify what should be done (see HowToDirection).

classes.label: HowToTool
classes.definition: A tool used (but not consumed) when performing instructions for how to achieve a result.

classes.label: HyperToc
classes.definition: A HyperToc represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. Items in the table of contents are indicated using the [[tocEntry]] property, and typed [[HyperTocEntry]]. For cases where the same larger work is split into multiple files, [[associatedMedia]] can be used on individual [[HyperTocEntry]] items.

classes.label: HyperTocEntry
classes.definition: A HyperToEntry is an item within a [[HyperToc]], which represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. The media object itself is indicated using [[associatedMedia]]. Each section of interest within that content can be described with a [[HyperTocEntry]], with associated [[startOffset]] and [[endOffset]]. When several entries are all from the same file, [[associatedMedia]] is used on the overarching [[HyperTocEntry]]; if the content has been split into multiple files, they can be referenced using [[associatedMedia]] on each [[HyperTocEntry]].

classes.label: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration
classes.definition: IPTC "Digital Source" codes for use with the [[digitalSourceType]] property, providing information about the source for a digital media object. In general these codes are not declared here to be mutually exclusive, although some combinations would be contradictory if applied simultaneously, or might be considered mutually incompatible by upstream maintainers of the definitions. See the IPTC documentation for detailed definitions of all terms.

classes.label: ITNonprofitType
classes.definition: ITNonprofitType: Non-profit organization type originating from Italy.

classes.label: IceCreamShop
classes.definition: An ice cream shop.

classes.label: IgnoreAction
classes.definition: The act of intentionally disregarding the object. An agent ignores an object.

classes.label: ImageGallery
classes.definition: Web page type: Image gallery page.

classes.label: ImageObject
classes.definition: An image file.

classes.label: ImageObjectSnapshot
classes.definition: A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[ImageObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata (e.g. XMP, EXIF) the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

classes.label: ImagingTest
classes.definition: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes.

classes.label: IncentiveQualifiedExpenseType
classes.definition: The types of expenses that are covered by the incentive. For example some incentives are only for the goods (tangible items) but the services (labor) are excluded.

classes.label: IncentiveStatus
classes.definition: Enumerates a status for an incentive, such as whether it is active.

classes.label: IncentiveType
classes.definition: Enumerates common financial incentives for products, including tax credits, tax deductions, rebates and subsidies, etc.

classes.label: IndividualPhysician
classes.definition: An individual medical practitioner. For their official address use [[address]], for affiliations to hospitals use [[hospitalAffiliation]]. The [[practicesAt]] property can be used to indicate [[MedicalOrganization]] hospitals, clinics, pharmacies etc. where this physician practices.

classes.label: IndividualProduct
classes.definition: A single, identifiable product instance (e.g. a laptop with a particular serial number).

classes.label: InfectiousAgentClass
classes.definition: Classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Enumerated type.

classes.label: InfectiousDisease
classes.definition: An infectious disease is a clinically evident human disease resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents, like pathogenic viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi, protozoa, multicellular parasites, and prions. To be considered an infectious disease, such pathogens are known to be able to cause this disease.

classes.label: InformAction
classes.definition: The act of notifying someone of information pertinent to them, with no expectation of a response.

classes.label: InsertAction
classes.definition: The act of adding at a specific location in an ordered collection.

classes.label: InstallAction
classes.definition: The act of installing an application.

classes.label: InstantaneousEvent
classes.definition: An event with no duration, like for instance a computer log entry.

classes.label: InsuranceAgency
classes.definition: An Insurance agency.

classes.label: Intangible
classes.definition: A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things such as quantities, structured values, etc.

classes.label: Integer
classes.definition: Data type: Integer.

classes.label: InteractAction
classes.definition: The act of interacting with another person or organization.

classes.label: InteractionCounter
classes.definition: A summary of how users have interacted with this CreativeWork. In most cases, authors will use a subtype to specify the specific type of interaction.

classes.label: InternetCafe
classes.definition: An internet cafe.

classes.label: InvestmentFund
classes.definition: A company or fund that gathers capital from a number of investors to create a pool of money that is then re-invested into stocks, bonds and other assets.

classes.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
classes.definition: A type of financial product that typically requires the client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial return.

classes.label: InviteAction
classes.definition: The act of asking someone to attend an event. Reciprocal of RsvpAction.

classes.label: Invoice
classes.definition: A statement of the money due for goods or services; a bill.

classes.label: ItemAvailability
classes.definition: A list of possible product availability options.

classes.label: ItemList
classes.definition: A list of items of any sort—for example, Top 10 Movies About Weathermen, or Top 100 Party Songs. Not to be confused with HTML lists, which are often used only for formatting.

classes.label: ItemListOrderType
classes.definition: Enumerated for values for itemListOrder for indicating how an ordered ItemList is organized.

classes.label: ItemPage
classes.definition: A page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel.

classes.label: JewelryStore
classes.definition: A jewelry store.

classes.label: JobPosting
classes.definition: A listing that describes a job opening in a certain organization.

classes.label: JoinAction
classes.definition:
An agent joins an event/group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, JoinAction refers to joining a group/team of people.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be receiving updates.
* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be polling for updates.

classes.label: Joint
classes.definition: The anatomical location at which two or more bones make contact.

classes.label: LakeBodyOfWater
classes.definition: A lake (for example, Lake Pontrachain).

classes.label: Landform
classes.definition: A landform or physical feature. Landform elements include mountains, plains, lakes, rivers, seascape and oceanic waterbody interface features such as bays, peninsulas, seas and so forth, including sub-aqueous terrain features such as submersed mountain ranges, volcanoes, and the great ocean basins.

classes.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
classes.definition: An historical landmark or building.

classes.label: Language
