classes.definition: Natural languages such as Spanish, Tamil, Hindi, English, etc. Formal language code tags expressed in [BCP 47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) can be used via the [[alternateName]] property. The Language type previously also covered programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, which are now best represented using [[ComputerLanguage]].

classes.label: LearningResource
classes.definition: The LearningResource type can be used to indicate [[CreativeWork]]s (whether physical or digital) that have a particular and explicit orientation towards learning, education, skill acquisition, and other educational purposes. [[LearningResource]] is expected to be used as an addition to a primary type such as [[Book]], [[VideoObject]], [[Product]] etc. [[EducationEvent]] serves a similar purpose for event-like things (e.g. a [[Trip]]). A [[LearningResource]] may be created as a result of an [[EducationEvent]], for example by recording one.

classes.label: LeaveAction
classes.definition:
An agent leaves an event / group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

* [[JoinAction]]: The antonym of LeaveAction.
* [[UnRegisterAction]]: Unlike UnRegisterAction, LeaveAction implies leaving a group/team of people rather than a service.

classes.label: LegalForceStatus
classes.definition: A list of possible statuses for the legal force of a legislation.

classes.label: LegalService
classes.definition: A LegalService is a business that provides legally-oriented services, advice and representation, e.g. law firms.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

classes.label: LegalValueLevel
classes.definition: A list of possible levels for the legal validity of a legislation.

classes.label: Legislation
classes.definition: A legal document such as an act, decree, bill, etc. (enforceable or not) or a component of a legal act (like an article).

classes.label: LegislationObject
classes.definition: A specific object or file containing a Legislation. Note that the same Legislation can be published in multiple files. For example, a digitally signed PDF, a plain PDF and an HTML version.

classes.label: LegislativeBuilding
classes.definition: A legislative building—for example, the state capitol.

classes.label: LendAction
classes.definition:
The act of providing an object under an agreement that it will be returned at a later date. Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

Related actions:

* [[BorrowAction]]: Reciprocal of LendAction.

classes.label: Library
classes.definition: A library.

classes.label: LibrarySystem
classes.definition: A [[LibrarySystem]] is a collaborative system amongst several libraries.

classes.label: LifestyleModification
classes.definition: A process of care involving exercise, changes to diet, fitness routines, and other lifestyle changes aimed at improving a health condition.

classes.label: Ligament
classes.definition: A short band of tough, flexible, fibrous connective tissue that functions to connect multiple bones, cartilages, and structurally support joints.

classes.label: LikeAction
classes.definition: The act of expressing a positive sentiment about the object. An agent likes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

classes.label: LinkRole
classes.definition: A Role that represents a Web link, e.g. as expressed via the 'url' property. Its linkRelationship property can indicate URL-based and plain textual link types, e.g. those in IANA link registry or others such as 'amphtml'. This structure provides a placeholder where details from HTML's link element can be represented outside of HTML, e.g. in JSON-LD feeds.

classes.label: LiquorStore
classes.definition: A shop that sells alcoholic drinks such as wine, beer, whisky and other spirits.

classes.label: ListItem
classes.definition: An list item, e.g. a step in a checklist or how-to description.

classes.label: ListenAction
classes.definition: The act of consuming audio content.

classes.label: LiteraryEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Literary event.

classes.label: LiveBlogPosting
classes.definition: A [[LiveBlogPosting]] is a [[BlogPosting]] intended to provide a rolling textual coverage of an ongoing event through continuous updates.

classes.label: LoanOrCredit
classes.definition: A financial product for the loaning of an amount of money, or line of credit, under agreed terms and charges.

classes.label: LocalBusiness
classes.definition: A particular physical business or branch of an organization. Examples of LocalBusiness include a restaurant, a particular branch of a restaurant chain, a branch of a bank, a medical practice, a club, a bowling alley, etc.

classes.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
classes.definition: Specifies a location feature by providing a structured value representing a feature of an accommodation as a property-value pair of varying degrees of formality.

classes.label: Locksmith
classes.definition: A locksmith.

classes.label: LodgingBusiness
classes.definition: A lodging business, such as a motel, hotel, or inn.

classes.label: LodgingReservation
classes.definition: A reservation for lodging at a hotel, motel, inn, etc.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

classes.label: LoginAction
classes.definition: The action of logging into a device or application.

classes.label: LoseAction
classes.definition: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity.

classes.label: LymphaticVessel
classes.definition: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries lymph fluid unidirectionally toward the heart.

classes.label: Manuscript
classes.definition: A book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed.

classes.label: Map
classes.definition: A map.

classes.label: MapCategoryType
classes.definition: An enumeration of several kinds of Map.

classes.label: MarryAction
classes.definition: The act of marrying a person.

classes.label: Mass
classes.definition: Properties that take Mass as values are of the form '<Number> <Mass unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 kg'.

classes.label: MathSolver
classes.definition: A math solver which is capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems.

classes.label: MaximumDoseSchedule
classes.definition: The maximum dosing schedule considered safe for a drug or supplement as recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity.

classes.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
classes.definition: Enumeration(s) for use with [[measurementMethod]].

classes.label: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumeration of common measurement types (or dimensions), for example "chest" for a person, "inseam" for pants, "gauge" for screws, or "wheel" for bicycles.

classes.label: MediaEnumeration
classes.definition: MediaEnumeration enumerations are lists of codes, labels etc. useful for describing media objects. They may be reflections of externally developed lists, or created at schema.org, or a combination.

classes.label: MediaGallery
classes.definition: Web page type: Media gallery page. A mixed-media page that can contain media such as images, videos, and other multimedia.

classes.label: MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration
classes.definition: Codes for use with the [[mediaAuthenticityCategory]] property, indicating the authenticity of a media object (in the context of how it was published or shared). In general these codes are not mutually exclusive, although some combinations (such as 'original' versus 'transformed', 'edited' and 'staged') would be contradictory if applied in the same [[MediaReview]]. Note that the application of these codes is with regard to a piece of media shared or published in a particular context.

classes.label: MediaObject
classes.definition: A media object, such as an image, video, audio, or text object embedded in a web page or a downloadable dataset i.e. DataDownload. Note that a creative work may have many media objects associated with it on the same web page. For example, a page about a single song (MusicRecording) may have a music video (VideoObject), and a high and low bandwidth audio stream (2 AudioObject's).

classes.label: MediaReview
classes.definition: A [[MediaReview]] is a more specialized form of Review dedicated to the evaluation of media content online, typically in the context of fact-checking and misinformation. For more general reviews of media in the broader sense, use [[UserReview]], [[CriticReview]] or other [[Review]] types. This definition is a work in progress. While the [[MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration]] list reflects significant community review amongst fact-checkers and others working to combat misinformation, the specific structures for representing media objects, their versions and publication context, are still evolving. Similarly, best practices for the relationship between [[MediaReview]] and [[ClaimReview]] markup have not yet been finalized.

classes.label: MediaReviewItem
classes.definition: Represents an item or group of closely related items treated as a unit for the sake of evaluation in a [[MediaReview]]. Authorship etc. apply to the items rather than to the curation/grouping or reviewing party.

classes.label: MediaSubscription
classes.definition: A subscription which allows a user to access media including audio, video, books, etc.

classes.label: MedicalAudience
classes.definition: Target audiences for medical web pages.

classes.label: MedicalAudienceType
classes.definition: Target audiences types for medical web pages. Enumerated type.

classes.label: MedicalBusiness
classes.definition: A particular physical or virtual business of an organization for medical purposes. Examples of MedicalBusiness include different businesses run by health professionals.

classes.label: MedicalCause
classes.definition: The causative agent(s) that are responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in a medical condition, symptom or sign. In this schema, unless otherwise specified this is meant to be the proximate cause of the medical condition, symptom or sign. The proximate cause is defined as the causative agent that most directly results in the medical condition, symptom or sign. For example, the HIV virus could be considered a cause of AIDS. Or in a diagnostic context, if a patient fell and sustained a hip fracture and two days later sustained a pulmonary embolism which eventuated in a cardiac arrest, the cause of the cardiac arrest (the proximate cause) would be the pulmonary embolism and not the fall. Medical causes can include cardiovascular, chemical, dermatologic, endocrine, environmental, gastroenterologic, genetic, hematologic, gynecologic, iatrogenic, infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic, nutritional, obstetric, oncologic, otolaryngologic, pharmacologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, rheumatologic, toxic, traumatic, or urologic causes; medical conditions can be causes as well.

classes.label: MedicalClinic
classes.definition: A facility, often associated with a hospital or medical school, that is devoted to the specific diagnosis and/or healthcare. Previously limited to outpatients but with evolution it may be open to inpatients as well.

classes.label: MedicalCode
classes.definition: A code for a medical entity.

classes.label: MedicalCondition
classes.definition: Any condition of the human body that affects the normal functioning of a person, whether physically or mentally. Includes diseases, injuries, disabilities, disorders, syndromes, etc.

classes.label: MedicalConditionStage
classes.definition: A stage of a medical condition, such as 'Stage IIIa'.

classes.label: MedicalContraindication
classes.definition: A condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a certain medical therapy. Contraindications can be absolute (there are no reasonable circumstances for undertaking a course of action) or relative (the patient is at higher risk of complications, but these risks may be outweighed by other considerations or mitigated by other measures).

classes.label: MedicalDevice
classes.definition: Any object used in a medical capacity, such as to diagnose or treat a patient.

classes.label: MedicalDevicePurpose
classes.definition: Categories of medical devices, organized by the purpose or intended use of the device.

classes.label: MedicalEntity
classes.definition: The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine.

classes.label: MedicalEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerations related to health and the practice of medicine: A concept that is used to attribute a quality to another concept, as a qualifier, a collection of items or a listing of all of the elements of a set in medicine practice.

classes.label: MedicalEvidenceLevel
classes.definition: Level of evidence for a medical guideline. Enumerated type.

classes.label: MedicalGuideline
classes.definition: Any recommendation made by a standard society (e.g. ACC/AHA) or consensus statement that denotes how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Note: this type should be used to tag the actual guideline recommendation; if the guideline recommendation occurs in a larger scholarly article, use MedicalScholarlyArticle to tag the overall article, not this type. Note also: the organization making the recommendation should be captured in the recognizingAuthority base property of MedicalEntity.

classes.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
classes.definition: A guideline contraindication that designates a process as harmful and where quality of the data supporting the contraindication is sound.

classes.label: MedicalGuidelineRecommendation
classes.definition: A guideline recommendation that is regarded as efficacious and where quality of the data supporting the recommendation is sound.

classes.label: MedicalImagingTechnique
classes.definition: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes. Enumerated type.

classes.label: MedicalIndication
classes.definition: A condition or factor that indicates use of a medical therapy, including signs, symptoms, risk factors, anatomical states, etc.

classes.label: MedicalIntangible
classes.definition: A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things in the medical space.

classes.label: MedicalObservationalStudy
classes.definition: An observational study is a type of medical study that attempts to infer the possible effect of a treatment through observation of a cohort of subjects over a period of time. In an observational study, the assignment of subjects into treatment groups versus control groups is outside the control of the investigator. This is in contrast with controlled studies, such as the randomized controlled trials represented by MedicalTrial, where each subject is randomly assigned to a treatment group or a control group before the start of the treatment.

classes.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
classes.definition: Design models for observational medical studies. Enumerated type.

classes.label: MedicalOrganization
classes.definition: A medical organization (physical or not), such as hospital, institution or clinic.

classes.label: MedicalProcedure
classes.definition: A process of care used in either a diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive or palliative capacity that relies on invasive (surgical), non-invasive, or other techniques.

classes.label: MedicalProcedureType
classes.definition: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures.

classes.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
classes.definition: A complex mathematical calculation requiring an online calculator, used to assess prognosis. Note: use the url property of Thing to record any URLs for online calculators.

classes.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
classes.definition: Any rule set or interactive tool for estimating the risk of developing a complication or condition.

classes.label: MedicalRiskFactor
classes.definition: A risk factor is anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing or contracting a disease, medical condition, or complication.

classes.label: MedicalRiskScore
classes.definition: A simple system that adds up the number of risk factors to yield a score that is associated with prognosis, e.g. CHAD score, TIMI risk score.

classes.label: MedicalScholarlyArticle
classes.definition: A scholarly article in the medical domain.

classes.label: MedicalSign
classes.definition: Any physical manifestation of a person's medical condition discoverable by objective diagnostic tests or physical examination.

classes.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
classes.definition: Any feature associated or not with a medical condition. In medicine a symptom is generally subjective while a sign is objective.

classes.label: MedicalSpecialty
classes.definition: Any specific branch of medical science or practice. Medical specialities include clinical specialties that pertain to particular organ systems and their respective disease states, as well as allied health specialties. Enumerated type.

classes.label: MedicalStudy
classes.definition: A medical study is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health, including observational studies and interventional trials and registries, randomized, controlled or not. When the specific type of study is known, use one of the extensions of this type, such as MedicalTrial or MedicalObservationalStudy. Also, note that this type should be used to mark up data that describes the study itself; to tag an article that publishes the results of a study, use MedicalScholarlyArticle. Note: use the code property of MedicalEntity to store study IDs, e.g. clinicaltrials.gov ID.

classes.label: MedicalStudyStatus
classes.definition: The status of a medical study. Enumerated type.

classes.label: MedicalSymptom
classes.definition: Any complaint sensed and expressed by the patient (therefore defined as subjective) like stomachache, lower-back pain, or fatigue.

classes.label: MedicalTest
classes.definition: Any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes.

classes.label: MedicalTestPanel
classes.definition: Any collection of tests commonly ordered together.

classes.label: MedicalTherapy
classes.definition: Any medical intervention designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions, including both curative and palliative therapies. Medical therapies are typically processes of care relying upon pharmacotherapy, behavioral therapy, supportive therapy (with fluid or nutrition for example), or detoxification (e.g. hemodialysis) aimed at improving or preventing a health condition.

classes.label: MedicalTrial
classes.definition: A medical trial is a type of medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or medical procedures. In general, medical trials are controlled and subjects are allocated at random to the different treatment and/or control groups.

classes.label: MedicalTrialDesign
classes.definition: Design models for medical trials. Enumerated type.

classes.label: MedicalWebPage
classes.definition: A web page that provides medical information.

classes.label: MedicineSystem
classes.definition: Systems of medical practice.

classes.label: MeetingRoom
classes.definition:
A meeting room, conference room, or conference hall is a room provided for singular events such as business conferences and meetings (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_hall).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: MemberProgram
classes.definition: A MemberProgram defines a loyalty (or membership) program that provides its members with certain benefits, for example better pricing, free shipping or returns, or the ability to earn loyalty points. Member programs may have multiple tiers, for example silver and gold members, each with different benefits.

classes.label: MemberProgramTier
classes.definition: A MemberProgramTier specifies a tier under a loyalty (member) program, for example "gold".

classes.label: MensClothingStore
classes.definition: A men's clothing store.

classes.label: Menu
classes.definition: A structured representation of food or drink items available from a FoodEstablishment.

classes.label: MenuItem
classes.definition: A food or drink item listed in a menu or menu section.

classes.label: MenuSection
classes.definition: A sub-grouping of food or drink items in a menu. E.g. courses (such as 'Dinner', 'Breakfast', etc.), specific type of dishes (such as 'Meat', 'Vegan', 'Drinks', etc.), or some other classification made by the menu provider.

classes.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates several kinds of product return policies.

classes.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
classes.definition: A MerchantReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an [[Organization]], [[Product]], or [[Offer]].

classes.label: MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride
classes.definition: A seasonal override of a return policy, for example used for holidays.

classes.label: Message
classes.definition: A single message from a sender to one or more organizations or people.

classes.label: MiddleSchool
classes.definition: A middle school (typically for children aged around 11-14, although this varies somewhat).

classes.label: MobileApplication
classes.definition: A software application designed specifically to work well on a mobile device such as a telephone.

classes.label: MobilePhoneStore
classes.definition: A store that sells mobile phones and related accessories.

classes.label: MolecularEntity
classes.definition: Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.

classes.label: MonetaryAmount
classes.definition: A monetary value or range. This type can be used to describe an amount of money such as $50 USD, or a range as in describing a bank account being suitable for a balance between £1,000 and £1,000,000 GBP, or the value of a salary, etc. It is recommended to use [[PriceSpecification]] Types to describe the price of an Offer, Invoice, etc.

classes.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
classes.definition: A statistical distribution of monetary amounts.

classes.label: MonetaryGrant
classes.definition: A monetary grant.

classes.label: MoneyTransfer
classes.definition: The act of transferring money from one place to another place. This may occur electronically or physically.

classes.label: MortgageLoan
classes.definition: A loan in which property or real estate is used as collateral. (A loan securitized against some real estate.)

classes.label: Mosque
classes.definition: A mosque.

classes.label: Motel
classes.definition:
A motel.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: Motorcycle
classes.definition: A motorcycle or motorbike is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle.

classes.label: MotorcycleDealer
classes.definition: A motorcycle dealer.

classes.label: MotorcycleRepair
classes.definition: A motorcycle repair shop.

classes.label: MotorizedBicycle
classes.definition: A motorized bicycle is a bicycle with an attached motor used to power the vehicle, or to assist with pedaling.

classes.label: Mountain
classes.definition: A mountain, like Mount Whitney or Mount Everest.

classes.label: MoveAction
classes.definition:
The act of an agent relocating to a place.

Related actions:

* [[TransferAction]]: Unlike TransferAction, the subject of the move is a living Person or Organization rather than an inanimate object.

classes.label: Movie
classes.definition: A movie.

classes.label: MovieClip
classes.definition: A short segment/part of a movie.

classes.label: MovieRentalStore
classes.definition: A movie rental store.

classes.label: MovieSeries
classes.definition: A series of movies. Included movies can be indicated with the hasPart property.

classes.label: MovieTheater
classes.definition: A movie theater.

classes.label: MovingCompany
classes.definition: A moving company.

classes.label: Muscle
classes.definition: A muscle is an anatomical structure consisting of a contractile form of tissue that animals use to effect movement.

classes.label: Museum
classes.definition: A museum.

classes.label: MusicAlbum
classes.definition: A collection of music tracks.

classes.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
classes.definition: Classification of the album by its type of content: soundtrack, live album, studio album, etc.

classes.label: MusicAlbumReleaseType
classes.definition: The kind of release which this album is: single, EP or album.

classes.label: MusicComposition
classes.definition: A musical composition.

classes.label: MusicEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Music event.

classes.label: MusicGroup
classes.definition: A musical group, such as a band, an orchestra, or a choir. Can also be a solo musician.

classes.label: MusicPlaylist
classes.definition: A collection of music tracks in playlist form.

classes.label: MusicRecording
classes.definition: A music recording (track), usually a single song.

classes.label: MusicRelease
classes.definition: A MusicRelease is a specific release of a music album.

classes.label: MusicReleaseFormatType
classes.definition: Format of this release (the type of recording media used, i.e. compact disc, digital media, LP, etc.).

classes.label: MusicStore
classes.definition: A music store.

classes.label: MusicVenue
classes.definition: A music venue.

classes.label: MusicVideoObject
classes.definition: A music video file.

classes.label: NGO
classes.definition: Organization: Non-governmental Organization.

classes.label: NLNonprofitType
classes.definition: NLNonprofitType: Non-profit organization type originating from the Netherlands.

classes.label: NailSalon
classes.definition: A nail salon.

classes.label: Nerve
classes.definition: A common pathway for the electrochemical nerve impulses that are transmitted along each of the axons.

classes.label: NewsArticle
classes.definition: A NewsArticle is an article whose content reports news, or provides background context and supporting materials for understanding the news. A more detailed overview of [schema.org News markup](/docs/news.html) is also available.

classes.label: NewsMediaOrganization
classes.definition: A News/Media organization such as a newspaper or TV station.

classes.label: Newspaper
classes.definition: A publication containing information about varied topics that are pertinent to general information, a geographic area, or a specific subject matter (i.e. business, culture, education). Often published daily.

classes.label: NightClub
classes.definition: A nightclub or discotheque.

classes.label: NonprofitType
classes.definition: NonprofitType enumerates several kinds of official non-profit types of which a non-profit organization can be.

classes.label: Notary
classes.definition: A notary.

classes.label: NoteDigitalDocument
classes.definition: A file containing a note, primarily for the author.

classes.label: Number
classes.definition:
Data type: Number.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

classes.label: NutritionInformation
classes.definition: Nutritional information about the recipe.

classes.label: Observation
classes.definition: Instances of the class [[Observation]] are used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time. The principal properties of an [[Observation]] are [[observationAbout]], [[measuredProperty]], [[statType]], [[value] and [[observationDate]] and [[measuredProperty]]. Some but not all Observations represent a [[QuantitativeValue]]. Quantitative observations can be about a [[StatisticalVariable]], which is an abstract specification about which we can make observations that are grounded at a particular location and time. Observations can also encode a subset of simple RDF-like statements (its observationAbout, a StatisticalVariable, defining the measuredPoperty; its observationAbout property indicating the entity the statement is about, and [[value]] ) In the context of a quantitative knowledge graph, typical properties could include [[measuredProperty]], [[observationAbout]], [[observationDate]], [[value]], [[unitCode]], [[unitText]], [[measurementMethod]].

classes.label: Occupation
classes.definition: A profession, may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification.

classes.label: OccupationalExperienceRequirements
classes.definition: Indicates employment-related experience requirements, e.g. [[monthsOfExperience]].

classes.label: OccupationalTherapy
classes.definition: A treatment of people with physical, emotional, or social problems, using purposeful activity to help them overcome or learn to deal with their problems.

classes.label: OceanBodyOfWater
classes.definition: An ocean (for example, the Pacific).

classes.label: Offer
classes.definition:
An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service — for example, an offer to sell tickets to an event, to rent the DVD of a movie, to stream a TV show over the internet, to repair a motorcycle, or to loan a book.

Note: As the [[businessFunction]] property, which identifies the form of offer (e.g. sell, lease, repair, dispose), defaults to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell; an Offer without a defined businessFunction value can be assumed to be an offer to sell.

For [GTIN](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin)-related fields, see [Check Digit calculator](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/support/check_digit_calculator) and [validation guide](http://www.gs1us.org/resources/standards/gtin-validation-guide) from [GS1](http://www.gs1.org/).

classes.label: OfferCatalog
classes.definition: An OfferCatalog is an ItemList that contains related Offers and/or further OfferCatalogs that are offeredBy the same provider.

classes.label: OfferForLease
classes.definition: An [[OfferForLease]] in Schema.org represents an [[Offer]] to lease out something, i.e. an [[Offer]] whose [[businessFunction]] is [lease out](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut.). See [Good Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoodRelations) for background on the underlying concepts.

classes.label: OfferForPurchase
classes.definition: An [[OfferForPurchase]] in Schema.org represents an [[Offer]] to sell something, i.e. an [[Offer]] whose [[businessFunction]] is [sell](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell.). See [Good Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoodRelations) for background on the underlying concepts.

classes.label: OfferItemCondition
classes.definition: A list of possible conditions for the item.

classes.label: OfferShippingDetails
classes.definition: OfferShippingDetails represents information about shipping destinations. Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping rates for different destinations: One entity for Alaska/Hawaii. A different one for continental US. A different one for all France. Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping costs and delivery times. Two entities that are identical but differ in rate and time: E.g. Cheaper and slower: $5 in 5-7 days or Fast and expensive: $15 in 1-2 days.

classes.label: OfficeEquipmentStore
classes.definition: An office equipment store.

classes.label: OnDemandEvent
classes.definition: A publication event, e.g. catch-up TV or radio podcast, during which a program is available on-demand.

classes.label: OnlineBusiness
classes.definition: A particular online business, either standalone or the online part of a broader organization. Examples include an eCommerce site, an online travel booking site, an online learning site, an online logistics and shipping provider, an online (virtual) doctor, etc.

classes.label: OnlineMarketplace
classes.definition: An eCommerce marketplace.

classes.label: OnlineStore
classes.definition: An eCommerce site.

classes.label: OpeningHoursSpecification
classes.definition:
A structured value providing information about the opening hours of a place or a certain service inside a place.

 The place is __open__ if the [[opens]] property is specified, and __closed__ otherwise.

If the value for the [[closes]] property is less than the value for the [[opens]] property then the hour range is assumed to span over the next day.

classes.label: OperatingSystem
classes.definition: System software that manages computer hardware and software resources, and provides common services for computer programs.

classes.label: OpinionNewsArticle
classes.definition: An [[OpinionNewsArticle]] is a [[NewsArticle]] that primarily expresses opinions rather than journalistic reporting of news and events. For example, a [[NewsArticle]] consisting of a column or [[Blog]]/[[BlogPosting]] entry in the Opinions section of a news publication.

classes.label: Optician
classes.definition: A store that sells reading glasses and similar devices for improving vision.

classes.label: Order
classes.definition: An order is a confirmation of a transaction (a receipt), which can contain multiple line items, each represented by an Offer that has been accepted by the customer.

classes.label: OrderAction
classes.definition: An agent orders an object/product/service to be delivered/sent.

classes.label: OrderItem
classes.definition: An order item is a line of an order. It includes the quantity and shipping details of a bought offer.

classes.label: OrderStatus
classes.definition: Enumerated status values for Order.

classes.label: Organization
classes.definition: An organization such as a school, NGO, corporation, club, etc.

classes.label: OrganizationRole
classes.definition: A subclass of Role used to describe roles within organizations.

classes.label: OrganizeAction
classes.definition: The act of manipulating/administering/supervising/controlling one or more objects.

classes.label: OutletStore
classes.definition: An outlet store.

classes.label: OwnershipInfo
classes.definition: A structured value providing information about when a certain organization or person owned a certain product.

classes.label: PaintAction
classes.definition: The act of producing a painting, typically with paint and canvas as instruments.

classes.label: Painting
classes.definition: A painting.

classes.label: PalliativeProcedure
classes.definition: A medical procedure intended primarily for palliative purposes, aimed at relieving the symptoms of an underlying health condition.

classes.label: ParcelDelivery
classes.definition: The delivery of a parcel either via the postal service or a commercial service.

classes.label: ParentAudience
classes.definition: A set of characteristics describing parents, who can be interested in viewing some content.

classes.label: Park
classes.definition: A park.

classes.label: ParkingFacility
classes.definition: A parking lot or other parking facility.

classes.label: PathologyTest
classes.definition: A medical test performed by a laboratory that typically involves examination of a tissue sample by a pathologist.

classes.label: Patient
classes.definition: A patient is any person recipient of health care services.

classes.label: PawnShop
classes.definition: A shop that will buy, or lend money against the security of, personal possessions.

classes.label: PayAction
classes.definition: An agent pays a price to a participant.

classes.label: PaymentCard
classes.definition: A payment method using a credit, debit, store or other card to associate the payment with an account.

classes.label: PaymentChargeSpecification
classes.definition: The costs of settling the payment using a particular payment method.

classes.label: PaymentMethod
classes.definition:
A payment method is a standardized procedure for transferring the monetary amount for a purchase. Payment methods are characterized by the legal and technical structures used, and by the organization or group carrying out the transaction. The following legacy values should be accepted: 

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByBankTransferInAdvance
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByInvoice
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Cash
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#CheckInAdvance
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#COD
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DirectDebit
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#GoogleCheckout
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PayPal
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PaySwarm

Structured values, or [UNCE payment means](https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/PaymentMeans) are recommended or for newer annotations.

classes.label: PaymentMethodType
classes.definition: The type of payment method, only for generic payment types, specific forms of payments, like card payment should be expressed using subclasses of PaymentMethod.

classes.label: PaymentService
classes.definition: A Service to transfer funds from a person or organization to a beneficiary person or organization.

classes.label: PaymentStatusType
classes.definition: A specific payment status. For example, PaymentDue, PaymentComplete, etc.

classes.label: PeopleAudience
classes.definition: A set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g. who compose an item's target audience.

classes.label: PerformAction
classes.definition: The act of participating in performance arts.

classes.label: PerformanceRole
classes.definition: A PerformanceRole is a Role that some entity places with regard to a theatrical performance, e.g. in a Movie, TVSeries etc.

classes.label: PerformingArtsEvent
classes.definition:
Live performance Event of the performing arts (music, theatre, dance, acrobatics, spoken word), including performance art and performative sports (e.g. choreographed forms of martial arts, figure skating, competitive ballroom dancing).

Note: Use additionalType to differentiate between productions / shows (PerformanceWork, EventSeries), tours (EventSeries), and individual performances.

classes.label: PerformingArtsTheater
classes.definition: A theater or other performing art center.

classes.label: PerformingGroup
classes.definition: A performance group, such as a band, an orchestra, or a circus.

classes.label: Periodical
classes.definition: A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to continue indefinitely, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

classes.label: Permit
classes.definition: A permit issued by an organization, e.g. a parking pass.

classes.label: Person
classes.definition: A person (alive, dead, undead, or fictional).

classes.label: PetStore
classes.definition: A pet store.

classes.label: Pharmacy
classes.definition: A pharmacy or drugstore.

classes.label: Photograph
classes.definition: A photograph.

classes.label: PhotographAction
classes.definition: The act of capturing still images of objects using a camera.

classes.label: PhysicalActivity
classes.definition: Any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health and wellness. Includes activity that is part of daily living and routine, structured exercise, and exercise prescribed as part of a medical treatment or recovery plan.

classes.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
classes.definition: Categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification.

classes.label: PhysicalExam
classes.definition: A type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician.

classes.label: PhysicalTherapy
classes.definition: A process of progressive physical care and rehabilitation aimed at improving a health condition.

classes.label: Physician
classes.definition: An individual physician or a physician's office considered as a [[MedicalOrganization]].

classes.label: PhysiciansOffice
classes.definition: A doctor's office or clinic.

classes.label: Place
classes.definition: Entities that have a somewhat fixed, physical extension.

classes.label: PlaceOfWorship
classes.definition: Place of worship, such as a church, synagogue, or mosque.

classes.label: PlanAction
classes.definition: The act of planning the execution of an event/task/action/reservation/plan to a future date.

classes.label: Play
classes.definition: A play is a form of literature, usually consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance rather than just reading. Note: A performance of a Play would be a [[TheaterEvent]] or [[BroadcastEvent]] - the *Play* being the [[workPerformed]].

classes.label: PlayAction
classes.definition:
The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition or exercise.

Related actions:

* [[ListenAction]]: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.
* [[WatchAction]]: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content.

classes.label: PlayGameAction
classes.definition: The act of playing a video game.

classes.label: Playground
classes.definition: A playground.

classes.label: Plumber
classes.definition: A plumbing service.

classes.label: PodcastEpisode
classes.definition: A single episode of a podcast series.

classes.label: PodcastSeason
classes.definition: A single season of a podcast. Many podcasts do not break down into separate seasons. In that case, PodcastSeries should be used.

classes.label: PodcastSeries
classes.definition: A podcast is an episodic series of digital audio or video files which a user can download and listen to.

classes.label: PoliceStation
classes.definition: A police station.

classes.label: PoliticalParty
classes.definition: Organization: Political Party.

classes.label: Pond
classes.definition: A pond.

classes.label: PostOffice
classes.definition: A post office.

classes.label: PostalAddress
classes.definition: The mailing address.

classes.label: PostalCodeRangeSpecification
classes.definition: Indicates a range of postal codes, usually defined as the set of valid codes between [[postalCodeBegin]] and [[postalCodeEnd]], inclusively.

classes.label: Poster
classes.definition: A large, usually printed placard, bill, or announcement, often illustrated, that is posted to advertise or publicize something.

classes.label: PreOrderAction
classes.definition: An agent orders a (not yet released) object/product/service to be delivered/sent.

classes.label: PrependAction
classes.definition: The act of inserting at the beginning if an ordered collection.

classes.label: Preschool
classes.definition: A preschool.

classes.label: PresentationDigitalDocument
classes.definition: A file containing slides or used for a presentation.

classes.label: PreventionIndication
classes.definition: An indication for preventing an underlying condition, symptom, etc.

classes.label: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates different price components that together make up the total price for an offered product.

classes.label: PriceSpecification
classes.definition: A structured value representing a price or price range. Typically, only the subclasses of this type are used for markup. It is recommended to use [[MonetaryAmount]] to describe independent amounts of money such as a salary, credit card limits, etc.

classes.label: PriceTypeEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates different price types, for example list price, invoice price, and sale price.

classes.label: Product
classes.definition: Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.

classes.label: ProductCollection
classes.definition: A set of products (either [[ProductGroup]]s or specific variants) that are listed together e.g. in an [[Offer]].

classes.label: ProductGroup
classes.definition: A ProductGroup represents a group of [[Product]]s that vary only in certain well-described ways, such as by [[size]], [[color]], [[material]] etc. While a ProductGroup itself is not directly offered for sale, the various varying products that it represents can be. The ProductGroup serves as a prototype or template, standing in for all of the products who have an [[isVariantOf]] relationship to it. As such, properties (including additional types) can be applied to the ProductGroup to represent characteristics shared by each of the (possibly very many) variants. Properties that reference a ProductGroup are not included in this mechanism; neither are the following specific properties [[variesBy]], [[hasVariant]], [[url]].

classes.label: ProductModel
classes.definition: A datasheet or vendor specification of a product (in the sense of a prototypical description).

classes.label: ProfessionalService
classes.definition: Original definition: "provider of professional services."\n\nThe general [[ProfessionalService]] type for local businesses was deprecated due to confusion with [[Service]]. For reference, the types that it included were: [[Dentist]], [[AccountingService]], [[Attorney]], [[Notary]], as well as types for several kinds of [[HomeAndConstructionBusiness]]: [[Electrician]], [[GeneralContractor]], [[HousePainter]], [[Locksmith]], [[Plumber]], [[RoofingContractor]]. [[LegalService]] was introduced as a more inclusive supertype of [[Attorney]].

classes.label: ProfilePage
classes.definition: Web page type: Profile page.

classes.label: ProgramMembership
classes.definition: Used to describe membership in a loyalty programs (e.g. "StarAliance"), traveler clubs (e.g. "AAA"), purchase clubs ("Safeway Club"), etc.

classes.label: Project
classes.definition: An enterprise (potentially individual but typically collaborative), planned to achieve a particular aim. Use properties from [[Organization]], [[subOrganization]]/[[parentOrganization]] to indicate project sub-structures.

classes.label: PronounceableText
classes.definition: Data type: PronounceableText.

classes.label: Property
classes.definition: A property, used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing; equivalent to rdf:Property.

classes.label: PropertyValue
classes.definition: A property-value pair, e.g. representing a feature of a product or place. Use the 'name' property for the name of the property. If there is an additional human-readable version of the value, put that into the 'description' property.\n\n Always use specific schema.org properties when a) they exist and b) you can populate them. Using PropertyValue as a substitute will typically not trigger the same effect as using the original, specific property.

classes.label: PropertyValueSpecification
classes.definition: A Property value specification.

classes.label: Protein
classes.definition: Protein is here used in its widest possible definition, as classes of amino acid based molecules. Amyloid-beta Protein in human (UniProt P05067), eukaryota (e.g. an OrthoDB group) or even a single molecule that one can point to are all of type :Protein. A protein can thus be a subclass of another protein, e.g. :Protein as a UniProt record can have multiple isoforms inside it which would also be :Protein. They can be imagined, synthetic, hypothetical or naturally occurring.

classes.label: PsychologicalTreatment
classes.definition: A process of care relying upon counseling, dialogue and communication aimed at improving a mental health condition without use of drugs.

classes.label: PublicSwimmingPool
classes.definition: A public swimming pool.

classes.label: PublicToilet
classes.definition: A public toilet is a room or small building containing one or more toilets (and possibly also urinals) which is available for use by the general public, or by customers or employees of certain businesses.

classes.label: PublicationEvent
classes.definition: A PublicationEvent corresponds indifferently to the event of publication for a CreativeWork of any type, e.g. a broadcast event, an on-demand event, a book/journal publication via a variety of delivery media.

classes.label: PublicationIssue
classes.definition: A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog-schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

classes.label: PublicationVolume
classes.definition: A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered. It may represent a time span, such as a year.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog-schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

classes.label: PurchaseType
classes.definition: Enumerates a purchase type for an item.

classes.label: QAPage
classes.definition: A QAPage is a WebPage focussed on a specific Question and its Answer(s), e.g. in a question answering site or documenting Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

classes.label: QualitativeValue
classes.definition: A predefined value for a product characteristic, e.g. the power cord plug type 'US' or the garment sizes 'S', 'M', 'L', and 'XL'.

classes.label: QuantitativeValue
classes.definition: A point value or interval for product characteristics and other purposes.

classes.label: QuantitativeValueDistribution
classes.definition: A statistical distribution of values.

classes.label: Quantity
classes.definition: Quantities such as distance, time, mass, weight, etc. Particular instances of say Mass are strings like '3 kg' or '4 milligrams'.

classes.label: Question
classes.definition: A specific question - e.g. from a user seeking answers online, or collected in a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) document.

classes.label: Quiz
classes.definition: Quiz: A test of knowledge, skills and abilities.

classes.label: Quotation
classes.definition: A quotation. Often but not necessarily from some written work, attributable to a real world author and - if associated with a fictional character - to any fictional Person. Use [[isBasedOn]] to link to source/origin. The [[recordedIn]] property can be used to reference a Quotation from an [[Event]].

classes.label: QuoteAction
classes.definition: An agent quotes/estimates/appraises an object/product/service with a price at a location/store.

classes.label: RVPark
classes.definition: A place offering space for "Recreational Vehicles", Caravans, mobile homes and the like.

classes.label: RadiationTherapy
classes.definition: A process of care using radiation aimed at improving a health condition.

classes.label: RadioBroadcastService
classes.definition: A delivery service through which radio content is provided via broadcast over the air or online.

classes.label: RadioChannel
classes.definition: A unique instance of a radio BroadcastService on a CableOrSatelliteService lineup.

classes.label: RadioClip
classes.definition: A short radio program or a segment/part of a radio program.

classes.label: RadioEpisode
classes.definition: A radio episode which can be part of a series or season.

classes.label: RadioSeason
classes.definition: Season dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery.

classes.label: RadioSeries
classes.definition: CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery.

classes.label: RadioStation
classes.definition: A radio station.

classes.label: Rating
classes.definition: A rating is an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars.

classes.label: ReactAction
classes.definition: The act of responding instinctively and emotionally to an object, expressing a sentiment.

classes.label: ReadAction
classes.definition: The act of consuming written content.

classes.label: RealEstateAgent
classes.definition: A real-estate agent.

classes.label: RealEstateListing
classes.definition: A [[RealEstateListing]] is a listing that describes one or more real-estate [[Offer]]s (whose [[businessFunction]] is typically to lease out, or to sell). The [[RealEstateListing]] type itself represents the overall listing, as manifested in some [[WebPage]].

classes.label: ReceiveAction
classes.definition:
The act of physically/electronically taking delivery of an object that has been transferred from an origin to a destination. Reciprocal of SendAction.

Related actions:

* [[SendAction]]: The reciprocal of ReceiveAction.
* [[TakeAction]]: Unlike TakeAction, ReceiveAction does not imply that the ownership has been transferred (e.g. I can receive a package, but it does not mean the package is now mine).

classes.label: Recipe
classes.definition: A recipe. For dietary restrictions covered by the recipe, a few common restrictions are enumerated via [[suitableForDiet]]. The [[keywords]] property can also be used to add more detail.

classes.label: Recommendation
classes.definition: [[Recommendation]] is a type of [[Review]] that suggests or proposes something as the best option or best course of action. Recommendations may be for products or services, or other concrete things, as in the case of a ranked list or product guide. A [[Guide]] may list multiple recommendations for different categories. For example, in a [[Guide]] about which TVs to buy, the author may have several [[Recommendation]]s.

classes.label: RecommendedDoseSchedule
classes.definition: A recommended dosing schedule for a drug or supplement as prescribed or recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity.

classes.label: RecyclingCenter
classes.definition: A recycling center.

classes.label: RefundTypeEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates several kinds of product return refund types.

classes.label: RegisterAction
classes.definition:
The act of registering to be a user of a service, product or web page.

Related actions:

* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, RegisterAction implies you are registering to be a user of a service, *not* a group/team of people.
* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting to poll for updates from the object.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting updates from the object.

classes.label: RejectAction
classes.definition:
The act of rejecting to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

* [[AcceptAction]]: The antonym of RejectAction.

classes.label: RentAction
classes.definition: The act of giving money in return for temporary use, but not ownership, of an object such as a vehicle or property. For example, an agent rents a property from a landlord in exchange for a periodic payment.

classes.label: RentalCarReservation
classes.definition: A reservation for a rental car.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

classes.label: RepaymentSpecification
classes.definition: A structured value representing repayment.

classes.label: ReplaceAction
classes.definition: The act of editing a recipient by replacing an old object with a new object.

classes.label: ReplyAction
classes.definition:
The act of responding to a question/message asked/sent by the object. Related to [[AskAction]].

Related actions:

* [[AskAction]]: Appears generally as an origin of a ReplyAction.

classes.label: Report
classes.definition: A Report generated by governmental or non-governmental organization.

classes.label: ReportageNewsArticle
classes.definition: The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is a subtype of [[NewsArticle]] representing news articles which are the result of journalistic news reporting conventions. In practice many news publishers produce a wide variety of article types, many of which might be considered a [[NewsArticle]] but not a [[ReportageNewsArticle]]. For example, opinion pieces, reviews, analysis, sponsored or satirical articles, or articles that combine several of these elements. The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is based on a stricter ideal for "news" as a work of journalism, with articles based on factual information either observed or verified by the author, or reported and verified from knowledgeable sources. This often includes perspectives from multiple viewpoints on a particular issue (distinguishing news reports from public relations or propaganda). News reports in the [[ReportageNewsArticle]] sense de-emphasize the opinion of the author, with commentary and value judgements typically expressed elsewhere. A [[ReportageNewsArticle]] which goes deeper into analysis can also be marked with an additional type of [[AnalysisNewsArticle]].

classes.label: ReportedDoseSchedule
classes.definition: A patient-reported or observed dosing schedule for a drug or supplement.

classes.label: ResearchOrganization
classes.definition: A Research Organization (e.g. scientific institute, research company).

classes.label: ResearchProject
classes.definition: A Research project.

classes.label: Researcher
classes.definition: Researchers.

classes.label: Reservation
classes.definition: Describes a reservation for travel, dining or an event. Some reservations require tickets. \n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, restaurant reservations, flights, or rental cars, use [[Offer]].

classes.label: ReservationPackage
classes.definition: A group of multiple reservations with common values for all sub-reservations.

classes.label: ReservationStatusType
classes.definition: Enumerated status values for Reservation.

classes.label: ReserveAction
classes.definition:
Reserving a concrete object.

Related actions:

* [[ScheduleAction]]: Unlike ScheduleAction, ReserveAction reserves concrete objects (e.g. a table, a hotel) towards a time slot / spatial allocation.

classes.label: Reservoir
classes.definition: A reservoir of water, typically an artificially created lake, like the Lake Kariba reservoir.

classes.label: ResetPasswordAction
classes.definition: The action of resetting the password of a device or application.

classes.label: Residence
classes.definition: The place where a person lives.

classes.label: Resort
classes.definition:
A resort is a place used for relaxation or recreation, attracting visitors for holidays or vacations. Resorts are places, towns or sometimes commercial establishments operated by a single company (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: Restaurant
classes.definition: A restaurant.

classes.label: RestrictedDiet
classes.definition: A diet restricted to certain foods or preparations for cultural, religious, health or lifestyle reasons.

classes.label: ResumeAction
classes.definition: The act of resuming a device or application which was formerly paused (e.g. resume music playback or resume a timer).

classes.label: ReturnAction
classes.definition: The act of returning to the origin that which was previously received (concrete objects) or taken (ownership).

classes.label: ReturnFeesEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates several kinds of policies for product return fees.

classes.label: ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates several types of return labels for product returns.

classes.label: ReturnMethodEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates several types of product return methods.

classes.label: Review
classes.definition: A review of an item - for example, of a restaurant, movie, or store.

classes.label: ReviewAction
classes.definition: The act of producing a balanced opinion about the object for an audience. An agent reviews an object with participants resulting in a review.

classes.label: ReviewNewsArticle
classes.definition: A [[NewsArticle]] and [[CriticReview]] providing a professional critic's assessment of a service, product, performance, or artistic or literary work.

classes.label: RiverBodyOfWater
classes.definition: A river (for example, the broad majestic Shannon).

classes.label: Role
classes.definition: Represents additional information about a relationship or property. For example a Role can be used to say that a 'member' role linking some SportsTeam to a player occurred during a particular time period. Or that a Person's 'actor' role in a Movie was for some particular characterName. Such properties can be attached to a Role entity, which is then associated with the main entities using ordinary properties like 'member' or 'actor'.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/06/16/introducing-role/).

classes.label: RoofingContractor
classes.definition: A roofing contractor.

classes.label: Room
classes.definition:
A room is a distinguishable space within a structure, usually separated from other spaces by interior walls (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

classes.label: RsvpAction
classes.definition: The act of notifying an event organizer as to whether you expect to attend the event.

classes.label: RsvpResponseType
classes.definition: RsvpResponseType is an enumeration type whose instances represent responding to an RSVP request.

classes.label: RuntimePlatform
classes.definition: Specialized software environment that provides the essential infrastructure, libraries, and services required to execute a program.

classes.label: SaleEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Sales event.

classes.label: SatiricalArticle
classes.definition: An [[Article]] whose content is primarily [[satirical]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire) in nature, i.e. unlikely to be literally true. A satirical article is sometimes but not necessarily also a [[NewsArticle]]. [[ScholarlyArticle]]s are also sometimes satirized.

classes.label: Schedule
classes.definition: A schedule defines a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring [[Event]]. At a minimum a schedule will specify [[repeatFrequency]] which describes the interval between occurrences of the event. Additional information can be provided to specify the schedule more precisely. This includes identifying the day(s) of the week or month when the recurring event will take place, in addition to its start and end time. Schedules may also have start and end dates to indicate when they are active, e.g. to define a limited calendar of events.

classes.label: ScheduleAction
classes.definition:
Scheduling future actions, events, or tasks.

Related actions:

* [[ReserveAction]]: Unlike ReserveAction, ScheduleAction allocates future actions (e.g. an event, a task, etc) towards a time slot / spatial allocation.

classes.label: ScholarlyArticle
classes.definition: A scholarly article.

classes.label: School
classes.definition: A school.

classes.label: SchoolDistrict
classes.definition: A School District is an administrative area for the administration of schools.

classes.label: ScreeningEvent
classes.definition: A screening of a movie or other video.

classes.label: Sculpture
classes.definition: A piece of sculpture.

classes.label: SeaBodyOfWater
classes.definition: A sea (for example, the Caspian sea).

classes.label: SearchAction
classes.definition:
The act of searching for an object.

Related actions:

* [[FindAction]]: SearchAction generally leads to a FindAction, but not necessarily.

classes.label: SearchRescueOrganization
classes.definition: A Search and Rescue organization of some kind.

classes.label: SearchResultsPage
classes.definition: Web page type: Search results page.

classes.label: Season
classes.definition: A media season, e.g. TV, radio, video game etc.

classes.label: Seat
classes.definition: Used to describe a seat, such as a reserved seat in an event reservation.

classes.label: SeekToAction
classes.definition: This is the [[Action]] of navigating to a specific [[startOffset]] timestamp within a [[VideoObject]], typically represented with a URL template structure.

classes.label: SelfStorage
classes.definition: A self-storage facility.

classes.label: SellAction
classes.definition: The act of taking money from a buyer in exchange for goods or services rendered. An agent sells an object, product, or service to a buyer for a price. Reciprocal of BuyAction.

classes.label: SendAction
classes.definition:
The act of physically/electronically dispatching an object for transfer from an origin to a destination. Related actions:

* [[ReceiveAction]]: The reciprocal of SendAction.
* [[GiveAction]]: Unlike GiveAction, SendAction does not imply the transfer of ownership (e.g. I can send you my laptop, but I'm not necessarily giving it to you).

classes.label: SequentialArt
classes.definition: An art forms that use images deployed in a specific order for the purpose of graphic storytelling (i.e., narration of graphic stories) or conveying information. Examples of SequentialArt are Franco-Belgian Bande Dessinée, Comics in the USA and 漫画 (Manga) in Japan.

classes.label: Series
classes.definition: A Series in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. See also [[CreativeWorkSeries]], [[EventSeries]].

classes.label: Service
classes.definition: A service provided by an organization, e.g. delivery service, print services, etc.

classes.label: ServiceChannel
classes.definition: A means for accessing a service, e.g. a government office location, web site, or phone number.

classes.label: ServicePeriod
classes.definition: ServicePeriod represents a duration with some constraints about cutoff time and business days. This is used e.g. in shipping for handling times or transit time.

classes.label: ShareAction
classes.definition: The act of distributing content to people for their amusement or edification.

classes.label: SheetMusic
classes.definition: Printed music, as opposed to performed or recorded music.

classes.label: ShippingConditions
classes.definition: ShippingConditions represent a set of constraints and information about the conditions of shipping a product. Such conditions may apply to only a subset of the products being shipped, depending on aspects of the product like weight, size, price, destination, and others. All the specified conditions must be met for this ShippingConditions to apply.

classes.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
classes.definition: ShippingDeliveryTime provides various pieces of information about delivery times for shipping.

classes.label: ShippingRateSettings
classes.definition: A ShippingRateSettings represents re-usable pieces of shipping information. It is designed for publication on an URL that may be referenced via the [[shippingSettingsLink]] property of an [[OfferShippingDetails]]. Several occurrences can be published, distinguished and matched (i.e. identified/referenced) by their different values for [[shippingLabel]].

classes.label: ShippingService
classes.definition: ShippingService represents the criteria used to determine if and how an offer could be shipped to a customer.

classes.label: ShoeStore
classes.definition: A shoe store.

classes.label: ShoppingCenter
classes.definition: A shopping center or mall.

classes.label: ShortStory
classes.definition: Short story or tale. A brief work of literature, usually written in narrative prose.

classes.label: SingleFamilyResidence
classes.definition: Residence type: Single-family home.

classes.label: SiteNavigationElement
classes.definition: A navigation element of the page.

classes.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates common size groups for various product categories.

classes.label: SizeSpecification
classes.definition: Size related properties of a product, typically a size code ([[name]]) and optionally a [[sizeSystem]], [[sizeGroup]], and product measurements ([[hasMeasurement]]). In addition, the intended audience can be defined through [[suggestedAge]], [[suggestedGender]], and suggested body measurements ([[suggestedMeasurement]]).

classes.label: SizeSystemEnumeration
classes.definition: Enumerates common size systems for different categories of products, for example "EN-13402" or "UK" for wearables or "Imperial" for screws.

classes.label: SkiResort
classes.definition: A ski resort.

classes.label: SocialEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Social event.

classes.label: SocialMediaPosting
classes.definition: A post to a social media platform, including blog posts, tweets, Facebook posts, etc.

classes.label: SoftwareApplication
classes.definition: A software application.

classes.label: SoftwareSourceCode
classes.definition: Computer programming source code. Example: Full (compile ready) solutions, code snippet samples, scripts, templates.

classes.label: SolveMathAction
classes.definition: The action that takes in a math expression and directs users to a page potentially capable of solving/simplifying that expression.

classes.label: SomeProducts
classes.definition: A placeholder for multiple similar products of the same kind.

classes.label: SpeakableSpecification
classes.definition: A SpeakableSpecification indicates (typically via [[xpath]] or [[cssSelector]]) sections of a document that are highlighted as particularly [[speakable]]. Instances of this type are expected to be used primarily as values of the [[speakable]] property.

classes.label: SpecialAnnouncement
classes.definition: A SpecialAnnouncement combines a simple date-stamped textual information update with contextualized Web links and other structured data. It represents an information update made by a locally-oriented organization, for example schools, pharmacies, healthcare providers, community groups, police, local government. For work in progress guidelines on Coronavirus-related markup see [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14ikaGCKxo50rRM7nvKSlbUpjyIk2WMQd3IkB1lItlrM/edit#). The motivating scenario for SpecialAnnouncement is the [Coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_coronavirus_pandemic), and the initial vocabulary is oriented to this urgent situation. Schema.org expect to improve the markup iteratively as it is deployed and as feedback emerges from use. In addition to our usual [Github entry](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2490), feedback comments can also be provided in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fpdFFxk8s87CWwACs53SGkYv3aafSxz_DTtOQxMrBJQ/edit#). While this schema is designed to communicate urgent crisis-related information, it is not the same as an emergency warning technology like [CAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Alerting_Protocol), although there may be overlaps. The intent is to cover the kinds of everyday practical information being posted to existing websites during an emergency situation. Several kinds of information can be provided: We encourage the provision of "name", "text", "datePosted", "expires" (if appropriate), "category" and "url" as a simple baseline. It is important to provide a value for "category" where possible, most ideally as a well known URL from Wikipedia or Wikidata. In the case of the 2019-2020 Coronavirus pandemic, this should be "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019-20\_coronavirus\_pandemic" or "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q81068910". For many of the possible properties, values can either be simple links or an inline description, depending on whether a summary is available. For a link, provide just the URL of the appropriate page as the property's value. For an inline description, use a [[WebContent]] type, and provide the url as a property of that, alongside at least a simple "[[text]]" summary of the page. It is unlikely that a single SpecialAnnouncement will need all of the possible properties simultaneously. We expect that in many cases the page referenced might contain more specialized structured data, e.g. contact info, [[openingHours]], [[Event]], [[FAQPage]] etc. By linking to those pages from a [[SpecialAnnouncement]] you can help make it clearer that the events are related to the situation (e.g. Coronavirus) indicated by the [[category]] property of the [[SpecialAnnouncement]]. Many [[SpecialAnnouncement]]s will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use [[spatialCoverage]] for the region, and [[announcementLocation]] to indicate specific [[LocalBusiness]]es and [[CivicStructure]]s. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both [[spatialCoverage]] and [[announcementLocation]]. The [[about]] property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using [[about]] only for representing non-location entities (e.g. a [[Course]] or a [[RadioStation]]). For places, use [[announcementLocation]] and [[spatialCoverage]]. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of [[about]] for locations too. The basic content of [[SpecialAnnouncement]] is similar to that of an [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSS) or [Atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(Web_standard)) feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting [[SpecialAnnouncement]] updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed with the [[webFeed]] property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline [[DataFeed]] object, with [[encodingFormat]] providing media type information, e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml".

classes.label: Specialty
classes.definition: Any branch of a field in which people typically develop specific expertise, usually after significant study, time, and effort.

classes.label: SportingGoodsStore
classes.definition: A sporting goods store.

classes.label: SportsActivityLocation
classes.definition: A sports location, such as a playing field.

classes.label: SportsClub
classes.definition: A sports club.

classes.label: SportsEvent
classes.definition: Event type: Sports event.

classes.label: SportsOrganization
classes.definition: Represents the collection of all sports organizations, including sports teams, governing bodies, and sports associations.

classes.label: SportsTeam
classes.definition: Organization: Sports team.

classes.label: SpreadsheetDigitalDocument
classes.definition: A spreadsheet file.

classes.label: StadiumOrArena
classes.definition: A stadium.

classes.label: State
classes.definition: A state or province of a country.

classes.label: Statement
classes.definition: A statement about something, for example a fun or interesting fact. If known, the main entity this statement is about can be indicated using mainEntity. For more formal claims (e.g. in Fact Checking), consider using [[Claim]] instead. Use the [[text]] property to capture the text of the statement.

classes.label: StatisticalPopulation
classes.definition: A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[StatisticalPopulation]] item that stands for that set of people. The properties [[numConstraints]] and [[constraintProperty]] are used to specify which of the populations properties are used to specify the population. Note that the sense of "population" used here is the general sense of a statistical population, and does not imply that the population consists of people. For example, a [[populationType]] of [[Event]] or [[NewsArticle]] could be used. See also [[Observation]], where a [[populationType]] such as [[Person]] or [[Event]] can be indicated directly. In most cases it may be better to use [[StatisticalVariable]] instead of [[StatisticalPopulation]].

classes.label: StatisticalVariable
classes.definition: [[StatisticalVariable]] represents any type of statistical metric that can be measured at a place and time. The usage pattern for [[StatisticalVariable]] is typically expressed using [[Observation]] with an explicit [[populationType]], which is a type, typically drawn from Schema.org. Each [[StatisticalVariable]] is marked as a [[ConstraintNode]], meaning that some properties (those listed using [[constraintProperty]]) serve in this setting solely to define the statistical variable rather than literally describe a specific person, place or thing. For example, a [[StatisticalVariable]] Median_Height_Person_Female representing the median height of women, could be written as follows: the population type is [[Person]]; the measuredProperty [[height]]; the [[statType]] [[median]]; the [[gender]] [[Female]]. It is important to note that there are many kinds of scientific quantitative observation which are not fully, perfectly or unambiguously described following this pattern, or with solely Schema.org terminology. The approach taken here is designed to allow partial, incremental or minimal description of [[StatisticalVariable]]s, and the use of detailed sets of entity and property IDs from external repositories. The [[measurementMethod]], [[unitCode]] and [[unitText]] properties can also be used to clarify the specific nature and notation of an observed measurement.

classes.label: StatusEnumeration
classes.definition: Lists or enumerations dealing with status types.

classes.label: SteeringPositionValue
classes.definition: A value indicating a steering position.

classes.label: Store
classes.definition: A retail good store.

classes.label: StructuredValue
classes.definition: Structured values are used when the value of a property has a more complex structure than simply being a textual value or a reference to another thing.

classes.label: SubscribeAction
classes.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates pushed to.

Related actions:

* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, SubscribeAction implies that the subscriber acts as a passive agent being constantly/actively pushed for updates.
* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.

classes.label: Substance
classes.definition: Any matter of defined composition that has discrete existence, whose origin may be biological, mineral or chemical.

classes.label: SubwayStation
classes.definition: A subway station.

classes.label: Suite
classes.definition:
