Serious adverse outcomes include those that are life-threatening; result in death, disability, or permanent damage; require hospitalization or prolong existing hospitalization; cause congenital anomalies or birth defects; or jeopardize the patient and may require medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of the outcomes in this definition.

properties.label: serverStatus
properties.definition: Status of a game server.

properties.label: serviceArea
properties.definition: The geographic area where the service is provided.

properties.label: serviceAudience
properties.definition: The audience eligible for this service.

properties.label: serviceLocation
properties.definition: The location (e.g. civic structure, local business, etc.) where a person can go to access the service.

properties.label: serviceOperator
properties.definition: The operating organization, if different from the provider. This enables the representation of services that are provided by an organization, but operated by another organization like a subcontractor.

properties.label: serviceOutput
properties.definition: The tangible thing generated by the service, e.g. a passport, permit, etc.

properties.label: servicePhone
properties.definition: The phone number to use to access the service.

properties.label: servicePostalAddress
properties.definition: The address for accessing the service by mail.

properties.label: serviceSmsNumber
properties.definition: The number to access the service by text message.

properties.label: serviceType
properties.definition: The type of service being offered, e.g. veterans' benefits, emergency relief, etc.

properties.label: sharedContent
properties.definition: A CreativeWork such as an image, video, or audio clip shared as part of this posting.

properties.label: shippingConditions
properties.definition: The conditions (constraints, price) applicable to the [[ShippingService]].

properties.label: shippingDestination
properties.definition: indicates (possibly multiple) shipping destinations. These can be defined in several ways, e.g. postalCode ranges.

properties.label: shippingDetails
properties.definition: Indicates information about the shipping policies and options associated with an [[Offer]].

properties.label: shippingOrigin
properties.definition: Indicates the origin of a shipment, i.e. where it should be coming from.

properties.label: shippingRate
properties.definition: The shipping rate is the cost of shipping to the specified destination. Typically, the maxValue and currency values (of the [[MonetaryAmount]]) are most appropriate.

properties.label: sibling
properties.definition: A sibling of the person.

properties.label: siblings
properties.definition: A sibling of the person.

properties.label: signDetected
properties.definition: A sign detected by the test.

properties.label: signOrSymptom
properties.definition: A sign or symptom of this condition. Signs are objective or physically observable manifestations of the medical condition while symptoms are the subjective experience of the medical condition.

properties.label: size
properties.definition: A standardized size of a product or creative work, specified either through a simple textual string (for example 'XL', '32Wx34L'), a QuantitativeValue with a unitCode, or a comprehensive and structured [[SizeSpecification]]; in other cases, the [[width]], [[height]], [[depth]] and [[weight]] properties may be more applicable.

properties.label: sizeGroup
properties.definition: The size group (also known as "size type") for a product's size. Size groups are common in the fashion industry to define size segments and suggested audiences for wearable products. Multiple values can be combined, for example "men's big and tall", "petite maternity" or "regular".

properties.label: sizeSystem
properties.definition: The size system used to identify a product's size. Typically either a standard (for example, "GS1" or "ISO-EN13402"), country code (for example "US" or "JP"), or a measuring system (for example "Metric" or "Imperial").

properties.label: skills
properties.definition: A statement of knowledge, skill, ability, task or any other assertion expressing a competency that is either claimed by a person, an organization or desired or required to fulfill a role or to work in an occupation.

properties.label: sodiumContent
properties.definition: The number of milligrams of sodium.

properties.label: softwareAddOn
properties.definition: Additional content for a software application.

properties.label: softwareHelp
properties.definition: Software application help.

properties.label: softwareRequirements
properties.definition: Component dependency requirements for application. This includes runtime environments and shared libraries that are not included in the application distribution package, but required to run the application (examples: DirectX, Java or .NET runtime).

properties.label: source
properties.definition: The source or cause of the event.

properties.label: sourceOrganization
properties.definition: The Organization on whose behalf the creator was working.

properties.label: sourcedFrom
properties.definition: The neurological pathway that originates the neurons.

properties.label: spatial
properties.definition: The "spatial" property can be used in cases when more specific properties (e.g. [[locationCreated]], [[spatialCoverage]], [[contentLocation]]) are not known to be appropriate.

properties.label: spatialCoverage
properties.definition: The spatialCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the place(s) which are the focus of the content. It is a subproperty of contentLocation intended primarily for more technical and detailed materials. For example with a Dataset, it indicates areas that the dataset describes: a dataset of New York weather would have spatialCoverage which was the place: the state of New York.

properties.label: speakable
properties.definition: Indicates sections of a Web page that are particularly 'speakable' in the sense of being highlighted as being especially appropriate for text-to-speech conversion. Other sections of a page may also be usefully spoken in particular circumstances; the 'speakable' property serves to indicate the parts most likely to be generally useful for speech. The *speakable* property can be repeated an arbitrary number of times, with three kinds of possible 'content-locator' values: 1.) *id-value* URL references - uses *id-value* of an element in the page being annotated. The simplest use of *speakable* has (potentially relative) URL values, referencing identified sections of the document concerned. 2.) CSS Selectors - addresses content in the annotated page, e.g. via class attribute. Use the [[cssSelector]] property. 3.) XPaths - addresses content via XPaths (assuming an XML view of the content). Use the [[xpath]] property. For more sophisticated markup of speakable sections beyond simple ID references, either CSS selectors or XPath expressions to pick out document section(s) as speakable. For this we define a supporting type, [[SpeakableSpecification]] which is defined to be a possible value of the *speakable* property.

properties.label: specialOpeningHoursSpecification
properties.definition: The special opening hours of a certain place.\n\nUse this to explicitly override general opening hours brought in scope by [[openingHoursSpecification]] or [[openingHours]].

properties.label: specialty
properties.definition: One of the domain specialities to which this web page's content applies.

properties.label: speed
properties.definition:
The speed range of the vehicle. If the vehicle is powered by an engine, the upper limit of the speed range (indicated by [[maxValue]]) should be the maximum speed achievable under regular conditions.

Typical unit code(s): KMH for km/h, HM for mile per hour (0.447 04 m/s), KNT for knot

*Note 1: Use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate the range. Typically, the minimal value is zero.
* Note 2: There are many different ways of measuring the speed range. You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the [[valueReference]] property.

properties.label: spokenByCharacter
properties.definition: The (e.g. fictional) character, Person or Organization to whom the quotation is attributed within the containing CreativeWork.

properties.label: sponsor
properties.definition: A person or organization that supports a thing through a pledge, promise, or financial contribution. E.g. a sponsor of a Medical Study or a corporate sponsor of an event.

properties.label: sportsActivityLocation
properties.definition: A sub property of location. The sports activity location where this action occurred.

properties.label: sportsEvent
properties.definition: A sub property of location. The sports event where this action occurred.

properties.label: sportsTeam
properties.definition: A sub property of participant. The sports team that participated on this action.

properties.label: spouse
properties.definition: The person's spouse.

properties.label: stage
properties.definition: The stage of the condition, if applicable.

properties.label: starRating
properties.definition: An official rating for a lodging business or food establishment, e.g. from national associations or standards bodies. Use the author property to indicate the rating organization, e.g. as an Organization with name such as (e.g. HOTREC, DEHOGA, WHR, or Hotelstars).

properties.label: startOffset
properties.definition: The start time of the clip expressed as the number of seconds from the beginning of the work.

properties.label: statType
properties.definition: Indicates the kind of statistic represented by a [[StatisticalVariable]], e.g. mean, count etc. The value of statType is a property, either from within Schema.org (e.g. [[median]], [[marginOfError]], [[maxValue]], [[minValue]]) or from other compatible (e.g. RDF) systems such as DataCommons.org or Wikidata.org.

properties.label: status
properties.definition: The status of the study (enumerated).

properties.label: steeringPosition
properties.definition: The position of the steering wheel or similar device (mostly for cars).

properties.label: step
properties.definition: A single step item (as HowToStep, text, document, video, etc.) or a HowToSection.

properties.label: steps
properties.definition: A single step item (as HowToStep, text, document, video, etc.) or a HowToSection (originally misnamed 'steps'; 'step' is preferred).

properties.label: study
properties.definition: A medical study or trial related to this entity.

properties.label: studyDesign
properties.definition: Specifics about the observational study design (enumerated).

properties.label: studyLocation
properties.definition: The location in which the study is taking/took place.

properties.label: studySubject
properties.definition: A subject of the study, i.e. one of the medical conditions, therapies, devices, drugs, etc. investigated by the study.

properties.label: subEvent
properties.definition: An Event that is part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each of which is a subEvent of the conference.

properties.label: subEvents
properties.definition: Events that are a part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each subEvents of the conference.

properties.label: subOrganization
properties.definition: A relationship between two organizations where the first includes the second, e.g., as a subsidiary. See also: the more specific 'department' property.

properties.label: subReservation
properties.definition: The individual reservations included in the package. Typically a repeated property.

properties.label: subStructure
properties.definition: Component (sub-)structure(s) that comprise this anatomical structure.

properties.label: subTest
properties.definition: A component test of the panel.

properties.label: subTrip
properties.definition: Identifies a [[Trip]] that is a subTrip of this Trip. For example Day 1, Day 2, etc. of a multi-day trip.

properties.label: subjectOf
properties.definition: A CreativeWork or Event about this Thing.

properties.label: subtitleLanguage
properties.definition: Languages in which subtitles/captions are available, in [IETF BCP 47 standard format](http://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47).

properties.label: successorOf
properties.definition: A pointer from a newer variant of a product to its previous, often discontinued predecessor.

properties.label: sugarContent
properties.definition: The number of grams of sugar.

properties.label: suggestedAge
properties.definition: The age or age range for the intended audience or person, for example 3-12 months for infants, 1-5 years for toddlers.

properties.label: suggestedAnswer
properties.definition: An answer (possibly one of several, possibly incorrect) to a Question, e.g. on a Question/Answer site.

properties.label: suggestedGender
properties.definition: The suggested gender of the intended person or audience, for example "male", "female", or "unisex".

properties.label: suggestedMeasurement
properties.definition: A suggested range of body measurements for the intended audience or person, for example inseam between 32 and 34 inches or height between 170 and 190 cm. Typically found on a size chart for wearable products.

properties.label: suitableForDiet
properties.definition: Indicates a dietary restriction or guideline for which this recipe or menu item is suitable, e.g. diabetic, halal etc.

properties.label: superEvent
properties.definition: An event that this event is a part of. For example, a collection of individual music performances might each have a music festival as their superEvent.

properties.label: supersededBy
properties.definition: Relates a term (i.e. a property, class or enumeration) to one that supersedes it.

properties.label: supply
properties.definition: A sub-property of instrument. A supply consumed when performing instructions or a direction.

properties.label: supplyTo
properties.definition: The area to which the artery supplies blood.

properties.label: supportingData
properties.definition: Supporting data for a SoftwareApplication.

properties.label: syllabusSections
properties.definition: Indicates (typically several) Syllabus entities that lay out what each section of the overall course will cover.

properties.label: target
properties.definition: Indicates a target EntryPoint, or url, for an Action.

properties.label: targetCollection
properties.definition: A sub property of object. The collection target of the action.

properties.label: targetProduct
properties.definition: Target Operating System / Product to which the code applies. If applies to several versions, just the product name can be used.

properties.label: taxonRank
properties.definition: The taxonomic rank of this taxon given preferably as a URI from a controlled vocabulary – typically the ranks from TDWG TaxonRank ontology or equivalent Wikidata URIs.

properties.label: taxonomicRange
properties.definition: The taxonomic grouping of the organism that expresses, encodes, or in some way related to the BioChemEntity.

properties.label: teaches
properties.definition: The item being described is intended to help a person learn the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term.

properties.label: termDuration
properties.definition: The amount of time in a term as defined by the institution. A term is a length of time where students take one or more classes. Semesters and quarters are common units for term.

properties.label: thumbnail
properties.definition: Thumbnail image for an image or video.

properties.label: ticketedSeat
properties.definition: The seat associated with the ticket.

properties.label: timeRequired
properties.definition: Approximate or typical time it usually takes to work with or through the content of this work for the typical or target audience.

properties.label: timeToComplete
properties.definition: The expected length of time to complete the program if attending full-time.

properties.label: toLocation
properties.definition: A sub property of location. The final location of the object or the agent after the action.

properties.label: toRecipient
properties.definition: A sub property of recipient. The recipient who was directly sent the message.

properties.label: tocContinuation
properties.definition: A [[HyperTocEntry]] can have a [[tocContinuation]] indicated, which is another [[HyperTocEntry]] that would be the default next item to play or render.

properties.label: tocEntry
properties.definition: Indicates a [[HyperTocEntry]] in a [[HyperToc]].

properties.label: tongueWeight
properties.definition:
The permitted vertical load (TWR) of a trailer attached to the vehicle. Also referred to as Tongue Load Rating (TLR) or Vertical Load Rating (VLR).

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

properties.label: tool
properties.definition: A sub property of instrument. An object used (but not consumed) when performing instructions or a direction.

properties.label: torque
properties.definition:
The torque (turning force) of the vehicle's engine.

Typical unit code(s): NU for newton metre (N m), F17 for pound-force per foot, or F48 for pound-force per inch

* Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined (e.g. reference RPM) using the [[valueReference]] property.
* Note 2: You can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

properties.label: totalPaymentDue
properties.definition: The total amount due.

properties.label: totalPrice
properties.definition:
The total price for the reservation or ticket, including applicable taxes, shipping, etc.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

properties.label: totalTime
properties.definition: The total time required to perform instructions or a direction (including time to prepare the supplies), in [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).

properties.label: touristType
properties.definition: Attraction suitable for type(s) of tourist. E.g. children, visitors from a particular country, etc.

properties.label: track
properties.definition: A music recording (track)—usually a single song. If an ItemList is given, the list should contain items of type MusicRecording.

properties.label: tracks
properties.definition: A music recording (track)—usually a single song.

properties.label: trailer
properties.definition: The trailer of a movie or TV/radio series, season, episode, etc.

properties.label: trailerWeight
properties.definition:
The permitted weight of a trailer attached to the vehicle.

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

properties.label: trainingSalary
properties.definition: The estimated salary earned while in the program.

properties.label: transFatContent
properties.definition: The number of grams of trans fat.

properties.label: transitTime
properties.definition: The typical delay the order has been sent for delivery and the goods reach the final customer. In the context of [[ShippingDeliveryTime]], use the [[QuantitativeValue]]. Typical properties: minValue, maxValue, unitCode (d for DAY). In the context of [[ShippingConditions]], use the [[ServicePeriod]]. It has a duration (as a [[QuantitativeValue]]) and also business days and a cut-off time.

properties.label: translationOfWork
properties.definition: The work that this work has been translated from. E.g. 物种起源 is a translationOf “On the Origin of Species”.

properties.label: translator
properties.definition: Organization or person who adapts a creative work to different languages, regional differences and technical requirements of a target market, or that translates during some event.

properties.label: travelBans
properties.definition: Information about travel bans, e.g. in the context of a pandemic.

properties.label: trialDesign
properties.definition: Specifics about the trial design (enumerated).

properties.label: tributary
properties.definition: The anatomical or organ system that the vein flows into; a larger structure that the vein connects to.

properties.label: tripOrigin
properties.definition: The location of origin of the trip, prior to any destination(s).

properties.label: typeOfBed
properties.definition: The type of bed to which the BedDetail refers, i.e. the type of bed available in the quantity indicated by quantity.

properties.label: typeOfGood
properties.definition: The product that this structured value is referring to.

properties.label: typicalCreditsPerTerm
properties.definition: The number of credits or units a full-time student would be expected to take in 1 term however 'term' is defined by the institution.

properties.label: typicalTest
properties.definition: A medical test typically performed given this condition.

properties.label: underName
properties.definition: The person or organization the reservation or ticket is for.

properties.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
properties.definition: For an [[Organization]] (typically a [[NewsMediaOrganization]]), a statement about policy on use of unnamed sources and the decision process required.

properties.label: unsaturatedFatContent
properties.definition: The number of grams of unsaturated fat.

properties.label: usageInfo
properties.definition: The schema.org [[usageInfo]] property indicates further information about a [[CreativeWork]]. This property is applicable both to works that are freely available and to those that require payment or other transactions. It can reference additional information, e.g. community expectations on preferred linking and citation conventions, as well as purchasing details. For something that can be commercially licensed, usageInfo can provide detailed, resource-specific information about licensing options. This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses.

properties.label: usedToDiagnose
properties.definition: A condition the test is used to diagnose.

properties.label: usesDevice
properties.definition: Device used to perform the test.

properties.label: validFor
properties.definition: The duration of validity of a permit or similar thing.

properties.label: validForMemberTier
properties.definition: The membership program tier(s) an Offer (or a PriceSpecification, OfferShippingDetails, or MerchantReturnPolicy under an Offer) is valid for.

properties.label: validIn
properties.definition: The geographic area where the item is valid. Applies for example to a [[Permit]], a [[Certification]], or an [[EducationalOccupationalCredential]].

properties.label: value
properties.definition:
The value of a [[QuantitativeValue]] (including [[Observation]]) or property value node.

* For [[QuantitativeValue]] and [[MonetaryAmount]], the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
* For [[PropertyValue]], it can be 'Text', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

properties.label: valueReference
properties.definition: A secondary value that provides additional information on the original value, e.g. a reference temperature or a type of measurement.

properties.label: variableMeasured
properties.definition: The variableMeasured property can indicate (repeated as necessary) the variables that are measured in some dataset, either described as text or as pairs of identifier and description using PropertyValue, or more explicitly as a [[StatisticalVariable]].

properties.label: variesBy
properties.definition: Indicates the property or properties by which the variants in a [[ProductGroup]] vary, e.g. their size, color etc. Schema.org properties can be referenced by their short name e.g. "color"; terms defined elsewhere can be referenced with their URIs.

properties.label: vehicleEngine
properties.definition: Information about the engine or engines of the vehicle.

properties.label: vehicleSeatingCapacity
properties.definition: The number of passengers that can be seated in the vehicle, both in terms of the physical space available, and in terms of limitations set by law.\n\nTypical unit code(s): C62 for persons.

properties.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
properties.definition: Indicates whether the vehicle has been used for special purposes, like commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi. The legislation in many countries requires this information to be revealed when offering a car for sale.

properties.label: vehicleTransmission
properties.definition: The type of component used for transmitting the power from a rotating power source to the wheels or other relevant component(s) ("gearbox" for cars).

properties.label: vendor
properties.definition: 'vendor' is an earlier term for 'seller'.

properties.label: verificationFactCheckingPolicy
properties.definition: Disclosure about verification and fact-checking processes for a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] or other fact-checking [[Organization]].

properties.label: video
properties.definition: An embedded video object.

properties.label: warranty
properties.definition: The warranty promise(s) included in the offer.

properties.label: warrantyPromise
properties.definition: The warranty promise(s) included in the offer.

properties.label: warrantyScope
properties.definition: The scope of the warranty promise.

properties.label: webFeed
properties.definition: The URL for a feed, e.g. associated with a podcast series, blog, or series of date-stamped updates. This is usually RSS or Atom.

properties.label: weight
properties.definition: The weight of the product or person.

properties.label: weightTotal
properties.definition:
The permitted total weight of the loaded vehicle, including passengers and cargo and the weight of the empty vehicle.

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

properties.label: wheelbase
properties.definition: The distance between the centers of the front and rear wheels.\n\nTypical unit code(s): CMT for centimeters, MTR for meters, INH for inches, FOT for foot/feet.

properties.label: width
properties.definition: The width of the item.

properties.label: winner
properties.definition: A sub property of participant. The winner of the action.

properties.label: workExample
properties.definition: Example/instance/realization/derivation of the concept of this creative work. E.g. the paperback edition, first edition, or e-book.

properties.label: workFeatured
properties.definition: A work featured in some event, e.g. exhibited in an ExhibitionEvent. Specific subproperties are available for workPerformed (e.g. a play), or a workPresented (a Movie at a ScreeningEvent).

properties.label: workLocation
properties.definition: A contact location for a person's place of work.

properties.label: workPerformed
properties.definition: A work performed in some event, for example a play performed in a TheaterEvent.

properties.label: workPresented
properties.definition: The movie presented during this event.

properties.label: workTranslation
properties.definition: A work that is a translation of the content of this work. E.g. 西遊記 has an English workTranslation “Journey to the West”, a German workTranslation “Monkeys Pilgerfahrt” and a Vietnamese translation Tây du ký bình khảo.

properties.label: workload
properties.definition: Quantitative measure of the physiologic output of the exercise; also referred to as energy expenditure.

properties.label: worksFor
properties.definition: Organizations that the person works for.

properties.label: yearlyRevenue
properties.definition: The size of the business in annual revenue.

properties.label: yearsInOperation
properties.definition: The age of the business.

properties.label: yield
properties.definition: The quantity that results by performing instructions. For example, a paper airplane, 10 personalized candles.
